Tyler Herro dropped a career-high 50 — then his buzzer-beater was waved off by a fingertip

By Matt

Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points for the Bucks in Philadelphia, including 15 in the first quarter. He appeared to tie the game at the buzzer — but replays showed the ball was still on his fingertips when the horn sounded, and the 76ers escaped 132-129.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Tyler Herro had the game of his life on Saturday afternoon in Philadelphia — and it still wasn't enough.

Herro finished with a career-high 50 points on 15-of-23 shooting, including 7-of-12 from three and a perfect 13-of-13 from the line, plus 11 rebounds and seven assists in 40 minutes. His previous career high was 41. The Bucks noted afterward that he is the first player in NBA history to record at least 50 points, 11 rebounds, seven three-pointers and 65 percent shooting in a single game.

He set the tone immediately, scoring 15 points in the first quarter to help Milwaukee take a 30-29 lead after 12 minutes. He poured in 35 more after halftime, and by the closing minute he was carrying the Bucks' entire comeback on his back.

The ending

The final 20 seconds were as cruel as a basketball ending gets.

Herro converted a running layup with 19.2 seconds left — the basket that got him to 50 — and cut the Sixers' lead to 128-126. Rookie Brayden Burries, who had a career-high 26 points off the bench, then drilled a three with 4.8 seconds to go to make it a one-point game. Joel Embiid answered with two free throws on the other end, and with 1.5 seconds left the Bucks inbounded the ball to Herro.

His fallaway three went in at the buzzer. The building erupted. Then the officials went to the replay.

Replays showed the ball was still on Herro's fingertips as the horn sounded. The basket was overturned, the game was over, and Philadelphia walked away with a 132-129 win. Herro finished with 50 — not 53, and no overtime.

What it means for the Bucks

The loss was Milwaukee's 13th in a row, dropping the Bucks to 1-16. Herro is the first Bucks player to score 50 points since Giannis Antetokounmpo did it on November 13, 2024, against the Pistons — and Giannis now plays for Miami, which is how Herro ended up in Milwaukee in the first place.

There is no silver lining in a 13-game losing streak. But a career night like this one, in a game the Bucks had no business being in, is the kind of performance that reminds everyone what Herro is: one of the purest scorers in the league, and the one player on this roster who can win a game by himself on any given night.

The other side

Philadelphia survived because its stars did just enough. Embiid had 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists — one assist short of a triple-double — and LeBron James added 21 points, six rebounds and six assists. Tyrese Maxey chipped in 17, and all five Sixers starters scored in double figures. The win moved Philadelphia to 14-3.

Embiid made four late free throws in all, and everyone on the Sixers' sideline was relieved to see that Herro hadn't quite released his jumper in time.

NHL · Nov 21, 2026 · 4:44 PM ET

MacKinnon's injury is much worse than first thought — out 12 weeks, and the Winter Classic is gone

By Matt

The Avalanche thought they were losing their best player for a month. After a specialist visit, the timeline tripled — and Nathan MacKinnon will now miss the Winter Classic and the rest of 2026.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The new timeline

Nathan MacKinnon is out approximately 12 weeks.

Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar gave the update on Saturday, November 21, after practice, and it was nothing like the news Colorado was hoping for. MacKinnon saw a specialist after the team returned home, and the re-evaluation changed everything. What was first called at least a month is now three times that long, keeping the Avalanche's leading scorer out through December and January, with a return sometime in February.

Bednar said he expects MacKinnon to make a full recovery and does not anticipate the injury becoming a recurring issue. That is the one piece of good news in an update that otherwise lands like a gut punch.

How it happened

The injury came on November 12 against the Ottawa Senators. MacKinnon took a cross-check from Senators defenseman Artem Zub in the second period, went down grabbing his side, and left the game. He did not return.

At the time, the hope was a month. MacKinnon had played 20 games and still leads Colorado in scoring with 30 points — 10 goals and 20 assists — despite missing the last three. He is 31, a former Hart Trophy winner, and the engine of everything the Avalanche do offensively. Losing him for a month was already a problem. Losing him for the rest of the calendar year is a different season entirely.

The Winter Classic is off the table

The most visible casualty of the new timeline is the Winter Classic. Colorado plays the Utah Mammoth outdoors on December 31 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, the kind of showcase game built around stars — and the Avalanche will play it without theirs.

It is not just one game, either. Colorado does not play again until November 25, when Montreal comes to town, and the schedule from here is a long stretch of hockey without the player who drives the top line, the top power play, and most nights the outcome.

What it means for Colorado

The Avalanche have held up so far. They are 13-7-3 and third in the Central Division, and they have gone 2-1 since MacKinnon and Cale Makar went down in the same game against Ottawa. Makar, the top defenseman, was also hurt that night and is expected to be out about two weeks, until around Thanksgiving — a much shorter absence, and one the team can plan around.

MacKinnon is the harder one to plan around. There is no replacement for a point-a-game center who leads the team in scoring and plays in every situation. The Avalanche have depth, and the last three games showed they can win without him. But three games is not three months. The test now is whether a team built around its two stars can stay in the race while one of them watches from the press box until February.

He will be back. Bednar made that clear. The question is what the standings look like when he gets there.

Sports · Nov 21, 2026 · 1:21 PM ET

Harry Kane tore ankle ligaments 20 minutes into Bayern's draw with Cologne — and he's out for months

By Matt

Harry Kane tore the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle 20 minutes into Bayern Munich's 1-1 draw with Cologne. Surgery was a success, but Bayern say the Ballon d'Or winner is out for the next few months.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The diagnosis

Harry Kane is out for the next few months. Bayern Munich confirmed on Friday that the England captain tore the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle — a high ankle sprain — in the 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne, and he underwent surgery overnight.

"Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich's Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening," Bayern said in a statement. "This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich's medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months."

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl put a number on it shortly after the match, telling ARD's Sportschau programme that Kane would be out for three months, likely until February. The operation itself was a success, Bayern said.

How it happened

The injury came 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena, and there was nothing cynical about it. Michael Olise sent a low cross toward the back post, and Cologne defender Joel Schmied got to the ball first — then clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow-through. No foul was called.

Kane went down clutching his lower leg and writhed in pain. He got gingerly back to his feet and tried to carry on, but he was limping, and after treatment he signalled to the dugout and hobbled off alongside two physios. Tom Bischof came on in his place.

It was a brutal night for Bayern's attack all round. Olise was also forced off, at half-time, after a challenge from Tom Krauß caught him in the left leg. He was later seen on crutches, though Bayern said he has only a bruised forefoot and Eberl was hopeful it is nothing serious. "We believe and hope it's nothing serious," Eberl said.

On the pitch, Bayern fell behind before Nathaniel Brown's 37th-minute strike levelled it at 1-1, and that was how it stayed. Bayern remain top of the Bundesliga on 22 points, with Cologne on 10.

What he said

Kane broke his silence on social media after the surgery, and the message was pure Kane — disappointed, but already looking at the calendar.

"The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

"'Tough times don't last, tough people do' — my guy @edelman11 told me this one!

"Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut."

What it means for Bayern

That layoff would rule Kane out of 11 Bundesliga games, the DFB-Pokal round of 16 tie against Hertha Berlin, and all four of Bayern's remaining Champions League league-phase matches. Bayern's next match is against Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, November 25 — without their No. 9.

The timing could hardly be worse for a player who has been the centre of everything Bayern do since arriving from Tottenham in 2023. He has scored 156 goals for the club, won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup, and last month became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years. Two weeks ago he signed a new contract keeping him in Bavaria until June 2029, reportedly worth more than £400,000 a week — the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.

He had gone into the international break without a goal in his previous four matches for Bayern, but he scored twice for England in the 3-2 Nations League win over Spain — the same week he earned his record 126th cap to become England's most-capped player.

What it means for England

The injury reaches beyond Munich. England face Norway in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final in March — in Oslo on March 27, then at Wembley on March 30 — and Kane could be facing a race to be fully fit for it.

As Henry Winter put it on Sky Sports' Back Pages Tonight: "It's three months and, most immediately, it's Bayern Munich's concern. But England have the home and away Nations League quarter-finals against Norway in late March. The timeline would suggest he'll be back in that time, but thoughts with Thomas Tuchel tonight because he'll be absolutely concerned about this. He's such an important player. England's No 9."

Kane's month had been a rollercoaster even before Friday: the Ballon d'Or on October 26, the new contract on November 5, a record-extending 92nd England goal against Croatia on November 12, the record 126th cap against Spain on November 15. Now the last line of the month reads very differently — injured after 20 minutes against Cologne, and out for months.

The hope, for Bayern and for England, is the one Kane wrote himself: back fresh for the business end of the season.

Mets offer Tarik Skubal nine years, nearly $400 million — the biggest pitcher offer in baseball history

By Matt

The Mets have offered free-agent ace Tarik Skubal a nine-year deal worth nearly $400 million, a reported offer that would make him the highest-paid pitcher in baseball history — if he takes it.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The offer

The New York Mets have offered two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth nearly $400 million. The report comes from former Mets general manager Jim Duquette, now an MLB Network Radio analyst, who said Friday that multiple MLB sources confirmed the terms. Reuters, USA Today, and the New York Post have all carried the report.

No deal is done. This is an offer — the first reported one of Skubal's free agency — and the Mets are not the only team at the table.

What the money means

If Skubal takes it, the deal would make him the highest-paid free-agent pitcher in baseball history. The total would pass the 12-year, $325 million contract Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in December 2023. The average annual value, about $44.4 million, would top the $43.3 million the Mets themselves paid Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander, the current record for a free-agent starting pitcher.

Those numbers tell you how the Mets see him: not as a good arm to add, but as the ace their rotation has been missing.

Why the Mets are all in

New York entered the offseason without a veteran ace. Rookie Nolan McLean is the club's top returning starter, and the rest of the projected 2027 rotation is a mix of upside and question marks. The Mets met with Skubal in California on Monday, and owner Steve Cohen is expected to be "all in" on landing him, according to the Post's Jon Heyman.

Skubal turned 30 on Friday. He split 2026 between Detroit and Los Angeles after a midseason move, going 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA in 26 starts, and he won the Cy Young in back-to-back seasons, 2024 and 2025. Across 163 career games he owns a 3.02 ERA.

Who else is in it

The Dodgers, the incumbent after acquiring him in August, have met with Skubal, as have the Blue Jays and the Padres. MLB Network reported a fifth team met with him over Zoom. The Dodgers and Blue Jays remain in the hunt, and Skubal spoke after the Dodgers' postseason exit about his love for the city — so the Mets' offer is an opening move, not a finish.

What happens next

Skubal is expected to sign before a lockout that could begin in early December, which puts a clock on all of this. The Mets have set the market with a record number. Now the question is whether anyone tops it — or whether Skubal takes the biggest offer a pitcher has ever been handed.

Sports · Nov 21, 2026 · 9:15 AM ET

Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL celebrating a sack — and his season is over

By Matt

The Lions' best defender tore the ACL in his right knee jumping to celebrate a sack of Drake Maye in Munich. Detroit placed him on injured reserve, and Hutchinson says the leap that ended his season was his last one.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The diagnosis

Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore the ACL in his right knee, and his 2026 season is over. The Lions placed him on injured reserve on Wednesday, November 18, three days after the injury in Munich.

It is the second season-ending injury of his five years in Detroit. In 2024 he broke the tibia and fibula in his left leg against the Dallas Cowboys and missed the rest of that season. He came back and played all 17 regular-season games in 2025, then opened this season as the anchor of one of the league's best pass rushes.

How it happened

The play itself was a highlight. On the opening drive of Detroit's 35-10 win over the New England Patriots on November 15, Hutchinson beat the tackle, caught Drake Maye from behind on third down, and dragged him to the turf. It was a sack that forced a field goal.

Then came the celebration. Hutchinson leapt in the air, and when he landed his right knee buckled. He recoiled immediately, collapsed, and grabbed the knee before heading to the locker room. Detroit ruled him out in the third quarter. The same play cost New England its quarterback too — Maye stayed in Germany overnight for testing and was later diagnosed with a fractured right fibula.

There was no hit on the play that hurt Hutchinson. No pile, no twist, no contact at all after the whistle. He jumped, he landed wrong, and his season ended on the landing.

What he said

Hutchinson broke his silence on Thursday, November 19, with an Instagram post that was equal parts disbelief and defiance.

"I honestly can't believe it. I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me. But even something like this won't hold me back. I can ask why over and over again, but it'll never make sense. All I can do is surrender to the path. Only God knows why and I trust in Him. Very grateful for all of your prayers and well wishes. Two things I know for sure: That's the last time I go airborne and I always come back stronger. Hold down the fort til I'm back, boys."

Head coach Dan Campbell did not dress it up when he addressed the injury: "It stinks." Campbell said he expects Hutchinson to attack rehab the same way he did after the broken leg in 2024, and that surgery is expected within the next week or two.

What it means for Detroit

The timing is brutal for a team in first place. Detroit is 7-2 and tied for first in the NFC North, and Hutchinson was the headliner of a pass rush that defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard called not "a one-man band" — but he also told his unit plainly that they will miss him.

The numbers back up both halves of that. Through nine games Hutchinson had 24 combined tackles, six sacks and one forced fumble. The Lions are still the only team in the league with three players at six sacks, with Alim McNeill at six and a half and D.J. Wonnum at six, so the rush has depth. It just lost its best player, and its most feared one, for the rest of the year.

Detroit hosts Tampa Bay on Sunday, the first game of life without Hutchinson. Kerby Joseph was activated from the physically unable to perform list in the same round of moves that sent Hutchinson to injured reserve, so the defense gets a starter back even as it loses its star.

The celebration question

Hutchinson's injury has already changed behavior around the league. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, known for his backflip celebrations, said after hearing about it that fans may not see the flip much anymore, if at all. "It's hard to see," he said. "I'm saying yeah [no more]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me."

Celebrating big plays is part of the game and always will be. Hutchinson jumped hundreds of times and nothing happened — until the one time it did. That is what makes this one land the way it has: it was not a dirty hit or a freak collision. It was a sack, a leap, and a landing, and a season ended in between.

He has done this comeback before. The broken leg in 2024 was supposed to be the setback that defined him. Instead he came back, played every game in 2025, and put up 14.5 sacks. Now he has to do it again, and his own words say he will.

Red Sox non-tender Connor Wong, closing the book on the Mookie Betts trade

By Matt

The Red Sox non-tendered catcher Connor Wong on Friday, making him a free agent — and ending Boston's last link to the Mookie Betts trade.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Boston Red Sox non-tendered catcher Connor Wong on Friday, making him a free agent. The decision was telegraphed earlier in the week: Boston designated Wong for assignment on Wednesday to clear a roster spot after acquiring catcher Nick Fortes from the Tampa Bay Rays, and no team claimed him or traded for him in the meantime.

Wong is now free to sign with any club. He figures to land a backup job somewhere — teams are always in the market for catching depth.

How it got here

The writing was on the wall well before this week. Wong hit .190 with no home runs in 2025, and while he improved to .233 in 2026, he never recaptured his 2024 form. His role shrank further after Boston acquired Adley Rutschman from the Orioles before the 2026 trade deadline, and the Fortes trade — Fortes for 17-year-old right-hander Angel Roa — gave the Sox a new backup catcher with better defensive metrics and a lower strikeout rate.

The money played a part too. MLB Trade Rumors projected Wong for a roughly $2 million salary in arbitration for 2027, and Boston had a cheaper, optionable alternative already on the roster in Mickey Gasper. Rather than tender Wong and stash him in Triple-A, the Sox moved on.

Wong in Boston

Wong appeared in 425 games for the Red Sox across six seasons, hitting .243/.304/.372 with 27 home runs, 128 RBI and 158 runs scored in 1,386 plate appearances. His 2026 line was .233/.308/.348 with four home runs, 25 RBI and three steals in 238 plate appearances over 77 games.

He stuck around longer than anyone else from the deal that brought him to Boston — and that is the real story here.

The last piece of the Betts trade

Wong was the last remaining player Boston acquired in the February 2020 Mookie Betts trade. The full deal sent Betts and pitcher David Price to the Los Angeles Dodgers for outfielder Alex Verdugo, shortstop Jeter Downs and Wong.

The other two pieces are already gone. Verdugo, the headliner of the return, spent four seasons in Boston (2020–23), hitting .281 with 43 home runs across 493 games — solid, but never the star the Sox gave up. He has since played for the Yankees and Braves and signed a minor-league deal with the Padres before being released after season-ending shoulder surgery. Downs played all of 14 games for Boston and hasn't appeared in the majors since 2023.

Meanwhile, Betts signed a 12-year, $365 million extension with the Dodgers and has helped them to three World Series titles since the trade. The Red Sox have reached the playoffs three times in the six years since and haven't won a playoff series since the 2021 ALCS.

Wong's departure doesn't change any of that — but it does close the book. There is now nothing left on Boston's roster from the most debated trade in modern franchise history.

What's next

Wong is a 30-year-old catcher with six seasons of big-league experience, a University of Houston product who could draw interest from Houston among others. He won't be a starter anywhere, but as a backup with pop — 27 career home runs — he should find work quickly.

Puka Nacua suspended three games — and MCL surgery likely ends his season

By Matt

Puka Nacua was suspended three games by the NFL for violating the personal conduct policy, and a day later Sean McVay revealed the Rams star underwent MCL surgery that will sideline him for a couple of months.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The suspension

The NFL suspended Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua for three games on Thursday for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The suspension began immediately, and because Nacua is already on injured reserve, he can serve it while he rehabs — meaning it costs him no additional games beyond the ones he was already going to miss.

It does cost him money. Nacua will forfeit three game checks, roughly $961,167 according to NFL Network's Tom Pelissero, and he cannot practice or attend games during the suspension. He is eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14, the day after the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers. The league also warned him that any further violation of the policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, could bring additional and more substantial discipline, up to and including banishment.

The surgery

One day after the suspension came down, head coach Sean McVay delivered the news that actually ends Nacua's season. The 25-year-old underwent surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, November 17, and will be out for a couple of months. McVay would not rule out a playoff return entirely, but the Rams are operating on the expectation that he will not play again this season.

The timing made for a strange sequence: the NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone knee surgery when it imposed the suspension, ESPN reported. And according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Nacua's recovery timeline does not match up with a potential return for Super Bowl LXI either — his only path back this season would be a deep Rams playoff run, and even that looks like a long shot.

How he got here

Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains, along with a turf toe injury, on the Rams' final offensive snap of their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on November 8. He was placed on injured reserve on November 12, which requires a minimum four-game absence, and he had already missed the Week 10 win over Arizona before the suspension was announced. The Rams are on their bye this week, and his earliest possible return date was the Week 15 home game against the Dallas Cowboys on December 20.

The backstory

The suspension stems from a New Year's Eve 2025 incident that led to a civil lawsuit filed in March, in which a woman accused Nacua of biting her on the shoulder and making an antisemitic remark after a group dinner in Los Angeles. Nacua has denied the allegations and entered a rehab program in April. The ban was the result of a negotiated settlement between the NFL and the NFL Players Association, rather than a full hearing before Judge Sue L. Robinson.

The season he was having

Losing Nacua is a major blow to a Rams offense that was already shorthanded. He caught 70 passes on 93 targets for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games this season, adding 41 rushing yards and a rushing score. His final game before the injury was his best of the year: 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win over Washington.

The Rams sit at 6-4, two and a half games behind the 8-1 49ers in the NFC West, and they will play the next three games — Green Bay, Kansas City, and San Francisco — without their top receiver. Davante Adams is also still out with a hamstring injury, so the passing game is running on fumes heading into the stretch. And the timing stings beyond this season: Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract, on a base salary of $5.76 million, and is set to be an unrestricted free agent in 2027. A huge payday is still expected — it just will not come with a healthy finish to this season attached.

Dodgers acquire Royce Lewis from the Twins for Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza

By Matt

The Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Twins on Friday, sending right-hander Bobby Miller and 19-year-old catching prospect Francisco Espinoza to Minnesota.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The deal

The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins on Friday, the clubs announced. In return, Minnesota gets right-handed pitcher Bobby Miller and minor league catcher Francisco Espinoza.

Jon Heyman of the New York Post first reported that Lewis was headed to Los Angeles, and the Dodgers confirmed the trade on X shortly after. It is the first major move of the offseason for both clubs, and it swaps one former top prospect whose career has stalled for another.

Why the Dodgers did it

Lewis is a buy-low bet on talent that has never been in question. The 27-year-old was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 draft, and when healthy he has shown the power and flair that made him that pick. The problem has been the healthy part — he has struggled to stay on the field throughout his career.

What Los Angeles is buying is versatility as much as upside. Lewis played three positions in 2026, logging time at first base, second base, and third base, which gives the Dodgers a right-handed bat they can move around the infield as needed. He is under club control through 2028, so this is not a rental — it is a two-year window to see if a change of scenery and a winning clubhouse unlock the player Minnesota drafted first overall.

What the numbers say

Lewis finished 2026 hitting .227 with 15 home runs, 57 RBI, 51 runs scored, and 16 stolen bases across 125 games. The average was a career low, and the Twins had explored moving him ahead of Friday's deadline to tender him a contract — he was arbitration-eligible for the first time, with MLB Trade Rumors projecting a $5.1 million salary for 2027. The Dodgers will pay a 110 percent luxury tax on him, so he will cost them more than $10 million in actuality.

Miller, also 27, heads the other way after barely pitching in the majors this year. He made three relief appearances for Los Angeles in 2026, going 1-0 with a 3.68 ERA over 7.1 innings with eight strikeouts. That is a long way from his promising rookie season in 2023, when he went 11-4 with a 3.76 ERA, and injuries and inconsistency have kept him from building on it since. Espinoza, a 19-year-old catcher who reached A-ball this past season, is the lottery ticket in the deal.

Why the Twins did it

For Minnesota, this is about the money and the roster crunch as much as the return. Lewis was a non-tender candidate, and moving him now frees up that projected arbitration salary from a payroll the Twins are trying to trim. In exchange they get a 27-year-old arm in Miller who was once one of the best pitching prospects in baseball, plus a teenage catcher to develop. It is not a haul — Twins fans made that clear within minutes of the announcement — but it beats non-tendering Lewis for nothing.

What it means

Both teams are betting on a fresh start fixing what the old one could not. The Dodgers have made a habit of turning other teams' distressed assets into contributors, and Lewis, healthy and in a lineup where he does not have to carry the offense, is exactly the kind of player that model is built for. The Twins, meanwhile, are betting that Miller still has a major league arm in there somewhere. One of these teams is going to look smart by July. The other is going to hear about it.

Saints waive starting safety Justin Reid at his request

By Matt

The Saints granted captain Justin Reid's request for his release on Friday, ending a two-season stint in New Orleans and handing the starting safety job to Jordan Howden.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The New Orleans Saints officially waived starting safety Justin Reid on Friday afternoon, granting a release the veteran had requested earlier in the week. Head coach Kellen Moore confirmed the move after Reid posted a goodbye message on social media, thanking the city and the team.

"I love Justin, I felt like this was the best for everyone," Moore said.

Reid, 29, is a defensive captain and a nine-year veteran. His farewell was gracious and brief: "In life and sports, things don't always go the way you planned or hoped they would. Unfortunately this is one of those moments."

Why now

The reason, by all accounts, is playing time. Reid played nearly every defensive snap early in the season, but his share dropped over the past three games as the Saints began turning to Jordan Howden at safety. Howden, 26, has earned those opportunities, in Moore's words, and he will start when the 3-6 Saints visit the 7-2 Chicago Bears on Sunday.

Moore declined to say whether Reid's request came because New Orleans was planning to replace him in the lineup. He did not have to. Reid had not practiced Wednesday or Thursday, listed on the injury report for what the team termed a personal matter, and he was still listed as the starter on the Saints' official depth chart on Friday morning. By Friday afternoon, he was gone.

Reid's Saints tenure never matched the heights of the resume he arrived with. He was a key contributor on the Chiefs' Super Bowl LVII and LVIII championship teams and started the Super Bowl LIX loss to the Eagles. In New Orleans, he started all 24 games he played and posted 118 tackles with one interception — one takeaway in two seasons for a player brought in to make plays. A concussion in the October 25 game in Paris seemed to mark the turn; his snap share declined afterward and never came back.

The money

Because the release came after the trade deadline, Reid goes through waivers, which clear at 4 p.m. ET on Monday. Any claiming team would inherit roughly the remaining $578,000 of his 2026 salary, plus a non-guaranteed $9.25 million option year for 2027. The Saints absorb about $5.2 million in dead cap this season and $13.26 million in 2027.

If nobody claims him, he becomes a free agent on Monday afternoon — and a two-time Super Bowl champion safety with starting experience should not stay unemployed long.

What's next

For New Orleans, this is the second time in two seasons a team captain has asked out. Wide receiver Brandin Cooks was granted his release a year ago under similar circumstances. That is a pattern, and it is not a flattering one for a 3-6 team already looking toward next year.

For Reid, the ending is abrupt but not bitter, at least publicly. Moore kept the conversations private, praised Reid as a player and a person, and framed the split as mutual. Reid thanked the organization and the city. Everybody said the right things. The football truth is simpler: the Saints decided Jordan Howden was their safety of the future, and Reid decided he would rather find his future somewhere else.

Drake Maye fractured his right fibula, likely out for the rest of the regular season

By Matt

Tests revealed the ankle injury Drake Maye suffered in Munich was a fractured right fibula, and the defending-champion Patriots' season now rests on Tommy DeVito.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The diagnosis

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered a fractured right fibula in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss reported Friday. The injury is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he is able to return this year at all.

There is a small silver lining in the news. Maye will not need surgery, and tests showed no additional ligament damage, which leaves the door open — barely — for a late return if the Patriots are still in playoff contention. The Patriots have not officially announced the diagnosis themselves, and they are on their bye this week, so no injury status has to be reported yet.

How it happened

Maye went down on the opening drive of the 35-10 loss to Detroit on November 15, sacked by Lions defensive lineman Aidan Hutchinson. What was initially feared to be an ankle injury turned out to be worse. Maye stayed overnight in Germany for testing to determine whether he would need surgery.

It was a strange week of silence before Friday's news. The Patriots said almost nothing about their franchise quarterback for five days, and the vacuum did the talking. Now we know why.

Who plays quarterback now

Head coach Mike Vrabel has already made the call: backup Tommy DeVito takes over as the starter, with 2026 seventh-round pick Behren Morton serving as the No. 2 option. DeVito replaced Maye for the remainder of the Lions game.

There is a roster wrinkle behind the decision. The Patriots have only one injured-reserve return designation left to use this season, and Maye is a candidate for it under normal circumstances. New England may choose not to place him on IR at all, preserving the designation — and the possibility, however slim, that he plays again this year.

What it means for the season

The Patriots are 5-5 and one game out of a playoff berth, which makes the timing brutal. Their remaining schedule is unforgiving: four games against winning teams in the Bills, Vikings, Chiefs and Broncos, starting with a November 29 trip to face the Chargers in Los Angeles. They also just lost wide receiver A.J. Brown for multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, so DeVito inherits a thinner offense than the one Maye was running.

Maye's season line is the reason this hurts as much as it does. In 10 games he completed 65.6 percent of his passes for 2,330 yards with 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, good for a 97.0 passer rating. The third-year quarterback finished as the runner-up for the 2025 NFL MVP Award, and he becomes eligible for a contract extension after the 2026 season — a negotiation that just got a lot more complicated.

For now, the defending champions are a 5-5 team with a backup quarterback, a banged-up receiving corps, and a closing schedule full of contenders. The season is not over. It just got a lot harder to see how it ends well.

Manon Fiorot suspended three months by UFC after positive test for ostarine

By Matt

Manon Fiorot has accepted a three-month suspension after testing positive for low levels of ostarine at UFC Noche, with anti-doping officials tracing the result to contaminated supplements.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The suspension

Manon Fiorot has accepted a three-month period of ineligibility for a violation of the UFC Anti-Doping Policy, Combat Sports Anti-Doping (CSAD) announced Thursday, November 19.

Fiorot tested positive for low levels of ostarine, a prohibited substance in the class of Anabolic Agents, in an in-competition sample collected on September 12, 2026, at UFC Noche, where she fought Alexa Grasso at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona. Fiorot lost that bout by unanimous decision.

Why only three months

The short ban comes down to how the ostarine got there. CSAD traced the positive result to a set of supplements supplied by Fiorot's nutritionist during fight week — new to her routine, and contaminated. Investigators found no evidence of intentional use and no significant performance advantage.

Fiorot also gave CSAD her full cooperation, and a second sample she provided on October 19, before she was even notified of the adverse finding, came back negative — consistent with her account that she only used the supplements during fight week. The supplements were neither tested nor certified, so she still bears responsibility, but CSAD used its discretion to reduce the penalty.

What's next

Fiorot's period of ineligibility began on October 19, 2026, the date she was notified of her provisional suspension, and it expires on January 19, 2027, when she will be eligible to compete again. The Arizona State Boxing and Mixed Martial Arts Commission, which also holds jurisdiction over the UFC Noche bout, will recognize the suspension and impose no separate sanction.

The 36-year-old French fighter, ranked No. 4 in the women's flyweight division, does not currently have a fight booked. She is 13-3, and her lone UFC title shot to date came at UFC 315 in May 2025, when she dropped a unanimous decision to then-champion Valentina Shevchenko. A three-month layoff is about as light a landing as a failed test gets — and with the calendar on her side, she should be back in the mix early in 2027.

Sports · Nov 21, 2026 · 7:16 AM ET

A.J. Brown expected to miss multiple weeks with hamstring injury, the third injury of a lost Patriots season

By Matt

ESPN reports A.J. Brown is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury suffered in the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Lions in Munich — his third separate injury this season.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The news

A.J. Brown is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Mike Reiss reported Friday, adding another chapter to what has been a miserable first season in New England for the three-time All-Pro wide receiver.

The Patriots have not placed Brown on injured reserve. But Reiss reports that, were they to do so, he would be eligible to return for the Week 16 game against the Jets after missing four games — which reads like the rough timeline the team is working with.

How it happened

Brown went down in the third quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, after a 21-yard catch-and-run. He briefly tried to play through it, then left for the locker room and did not return.

It was his first game back after a two-game absence, and it lasted less than three quarters.

A season of three injuries

This is the third separate injury to sideline Brown this season. He suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Week 1 loss to the Seahawks that landed him on injured reserve for four games. Upon his return, a knee flare-up kept him out of games in Weeks 8 and 9. He came back in Week 10 only to pull his hamstring.

The production, when he has been on the field, has not matched the player New England thought it was getting: four games, 11 catches, 128 yards, zero touchdowns.

That is the return so far on a June trade that sent a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles. ESPN's Dan Orlovsky put the question bluntly on Friday: "did they get fleeced?"

What it means for the Patriots

The timing could hardly be worse. New England is 5-5 and on its Week 11 bye, one game behind the Cleveland Browns (6-4) for the third AFC wild-card spot, and the schedule out of the bye is unforgiving: the Chargers, Bills, Vikings, and Chiefs.

And Brown is not even the worst of Friday's news. Quarterback Drake Maye fractured his right fibula in the same loss to Detroit and is likely to miss the rest of the regular season, though he will not need surgery. The Patriots could be without their quarterback and their No. 1 receiver for the stretch run — with a backup quarterback, Tommy DeVito, and a rookie, Behren Morton, behind Maye on the depth chart.

The bye at least buys time. The question is whether there is anything left to save when Brown and Maye are healthy enough to come back.

TSL Bets: The Saturday parlay (~+377) — Towns OVER 37.5 PRA, Procházka moneyline at UFC Qatar

By Matt

Karl-Anthony Towns has cleared 37.5 points, rebounds and assists in 7 of his last 10, and Jiří Procházka is a live +160 underdog with championship experience against an unbeaten contender in his first main event. Two legs, about +377.

Leg 1 — the game

Portland Trail Blazers (10-5) at New York Knicks (9-6) — 7:30 PM ET, Madison Square Garden, New York, NBA TV

Knicks -5.5, total 217.5 (lines via FanDuel).

Injuries — Portland: F Deni Avdija QUESTIONABLE (left foot contusion — he has missed the last two games, and he is Portland's leading scorer at 24.2 points a game). G Ja Morant OUT (left hamstring strain, Grade 2 — out until around December 1). G/F Shaedon Sharpe OUT (right meniscus surgery — about six months). F Vit Krejci OUT (left ankle fracture). G Chris Youngblood OUT (right heel/foot bone bruise). C Robert Williams III day-to-day (rest) — expected to be available.

Injuries — New York: F OG Anunoby questionable (left calf tightness). G Jordan Clarkson OUT (right plantar fasciitis). Other reports list the Knicks as fully healthy, so the Anunoby designation is the one to watch.

Storylines: The Knicks are the defending champions, 9-6, and winners of three straight — twice over Toronto and a 102-99 win at Minnesota on Thursday after leading by 19 in the third quarter. Jalen Brunson leads them at 26.6 points a game, sixth in the league, and Karl-Anthony Towns is the second option. Portland is 10-5 under first-year coach Micah Nori with Damian Lillard back in the fold (20.9 points a game), on the fifth stop of a six-game road trip, chasing its first win in this series since November 2022. The frontcourt matchup is the edge: Portland's only true big is Donovan Clingan, with Williams day-to-day and Avdija questionable, and Towns has cleared 37.5 points, rebounds and assists in 7 of his last 10 while averaging 39.3. He landed on 38 on Thursday at Minnesota (22 points, 12 rebounds, 4 assists).

Leg 2 — the fight

Jiří Procházka (32-6-1) vs. Navajo Stirling (11-0) — UFC light heavyweight, 5 rounds, ~3:00 PM ET, ABHA Arena, Doha, main card 1:00 PM ET on Paramount+

Procházka +160, Stirling -192 — DraftKings via Wise Guy Team, prices checked November 21, 6:55 AM ET.

Weigh-ins: Both men hit 205 pounds on Friday, and the main event is official. The only miss on the 12-fight card was Tahir Abdullayev at 172 pounds, one over for his prelim against Jake Matthews — he forfeits 20 percent of his purse and the fight goes ahead at catchweight.

Camp/availability: Procházka returns for the first time since Carlos Ulberg knocked him out in the first round at UFC 327 in April, in a fight for the division's vacant title. Before that setback he knocked out Khalil Rountree Jr. in the third round and Jamahal Hill. Stirling trains at City Kickboxing alongside Ulberg — the man who just beat Procházka — and Procházka has said openly he didn't want this matchup at first, because Stirling is the lower-ranked fighter from the same camp. Stirling is 29 and has finished three straight opponents by knockout in 2026: Bruno Lopes, Ion Cuțelaba, and former champion Jan Błachowicz in the first round at UFC Belgrade in August. Saturday is his first UFC main event.

Storylines: This is a former champion as a +160 underdog. Procházka owns the championship experience — five-round fights, title-fight pressure, the walk to the cage as the hunted — and Stirling is in his first main event against his first former champion. The MMA Junkie staff picks back the dog, 7-4 for Procházka. The market disagrees: Stirling is a 62% favorite on the exchanges, and he has finished three straight by knockout this year, including a former champion in round one. The case for the dog is experience and proven five-round pedigree; the case for the favorite is that he just starched Błachowicz in a round.

The bet

Karl-Anthony Towns OVER 37.5 points + rebounds + assists (-120, FanDuel) + Jiří Procházka moneyline (+160, DraftKings) — about +377. A $10 ticket returns about $47.70.

Why these legs

Both legs clear on their own. Towns has cleared 37.5 PRA in 7 of his last 10 while averaging 39.3, and he just cleared it on Thursday with 38 — against a Portland frontcourt that is down to Clingan with Williams day-to-day and its leading scorer questionable. The line is 37.5 at -120, and the consensus line across books is 37.5. Procházka is the upside leg: a plus-money dog with a real path, not a lottery ticket — former champion, championship rounds on his record, staff picks 7-4 his way, and an opponent in his first main event. Neither leg depends on the other — different sport, different building, different afternoon. That is the juice rule working as intended: two real edges, one ticket, about +377 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites.

The honest caveats

Towns landed on 38 on Thursday, clearing by half a point, and one model puts the over at 37.5 at about 50% — the trend is the case here, not a model consensus. Portland's defense is seventh in the league, and if Avdija does play, the Blazers' offense stays dangerous enough to keep the Knicks honest late. On the fight side, Procházka was knocked out in the first round in April, and Stirling has finished three straight by knockout, including a former champion in round one — the favorite is favored for a reason, and a second straight early knockout loss is a live outcome. A parlay needs both legs, and either one can sink it alone.

The record

New Orleans Pelicans (5-12) at San Antonio Spurs (13-3)

Saturday, 8:00 PM ET — Frost Bank Center, San Antonio (DAZN)

NBA · Nov 21, 2026 · 3:09 AM ET

Harden passes Kobe with 51-point night

By Matt

James Harden dropped 51 on the Pacers to pass Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games in NBA history — at 37, in a season where he'd barely cracked 30 all year.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

James Harden turned back the clock on Friday night. The 37-year-old guard scored 51 points to lead the Cleveland Cavaliers past the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an Emirates NBA Cup game at Rocket Arena — and in doing so, he recorded his 26th career 50-point game, moving past Kobe Bryant into third place on the all-time list.

Harden shot 15-of-26 from the field, 7-of-11 from three, and a perfect 14-of-14 from the free-throw line, adding six rebounds and six assists in a season-high 40 minutes. It was his first 40-point game since November 22, 2025 — when he dropped 55 for the Clippers against Charlotte, two days shy of a full year earlier — and his best scoring night since joining Cleveland near last season's trade deadline, topping the 36 he put up against Chicago.

How the night unfolded

Harden signaled what was coming early, scoring 15 points in the first nine minutes as the teams fought to a 29-29 draw. He had 24 by halftime, but Cleveland still trailed early in the third before flipping the game for good: up 74-73 four minutes into the period, the Cavs ripped off a 21-4 run, with Harden scoring 13 of those points on a perfect 4-of-4 from the field.

The third quarter belonged to him outright — 18 points on 6-of-8 shooting — and his driving layup at the end of the period pushed the total to 42 and the lead to 105-83. Cleveland outscored Indiana 43-22 in the quarter.

The Cavaliers led by 24 early in the fourth quarter, but Indiana gradually cut into the margin. Harden's flagrant foul gave the Pacers two free throws and possession — Jarace Walker made both, then assisted an Obi Toppin dunk that brought Indiana within six with 2:03 left. Donovan Mitchell answered with a driving floater, and Harden closed it himself: a three with 57.9 seconds left made it 124-113, and two more free throws with 42.3 seconds left carried him past 50 and sealed the win. He scored seven of Cleveland's final nine points.

1st: 15; 29-29

2nd: 9; 62-61

3rd: 18; 105-83

4th: 9; 128-119

Mitchell added 20 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists. The win moved Cleveland to 2-1 in East Group B of the NBA Cup and 9-8 overall, with three wins in its last four.

Where the milestone sits in history

Only two players in NBA history have more 50-point games than Harden now does. Wilt Chamberlain leads the way with 118, and Michael Jordan sits second with 31. Bryant finished his career with 25, and Elgin Baylor rounds out the top five with 17.

The number is even more striking in context: Harden is one of only six players age 37 or older to ever score 50 in a game, joining Bryant, Jordan, LeBron James, Jamal Crawford and Steph Curry. At 37 years and 86 days, he is one of the oldest players ever to do it.

The night also moved him up another all-time list. It was his 346th career 30-point game, passing Allen Iverson and tying Dominique Wilkins for the 10th-most in NBA history. Only four guards have more: Jordan, Bryant, Oscar Robertson and Jerry West. And he has now scored 50 or more against 18 different teams, passing Jordan and Bryant, who each did it against 17.

In Cavaliers history, it was the 15th 50-point game by any player — Harden is just the sixth Cavalier ever to do it, and the first since Donovan Mitchell's 71-point night against Chicago on January 2, 2023.

Why this one hit different

This wasn't a star padding a hot streak. Harden entered Friday averaging 16.2 points per game on 38.5% shooting — a career low — and had cracked 25 points just once all season, a 32-point night at Madison Square Garden on November 11. His previous season high was that 32. He blew past it by the third quarter.

The milestone clearly meant something to him afterward. Asked about passing Bryant, Harden called him "my idol" — "the person I watched growing up. The way he cared about the game and the effort he put in is something special. So, we miss him. We miss him a lot."

Harden signed a three-year, $96 million deal to stay in Cleveland this past summer, so the chase isn't over — Jordan's mark of 31 is now five away, and a healthy season of nights like this one puts it within reach. For now, though, the story is simpler: a 37-year-old in his 18th season, in a year where the scoring had mostly dried up, went out and reminded everyone what the Beard used to do every other week.

Sports · Nov 20, 2026 · 8:37 PM ET

Colts release Daniel Jones after 26-3 loss in Houston, hand the job back to Anthony Richardson

By Matt

The Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday, one day after a 26-3 loss in Houston, and named Anthony Richardson the starter for the November 29 game against the Giants.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The move

The Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday, head coach Shane Steichen announced, ending an 11-game stint that started with an $88 million contract and ended with the worst passing numbers of Jones's career.

Anthony Richardson is the starter now. His first start since the 2024 season comes on Sunday, November 29, when the Colts host the New York Giants — the team that drafted Jones and where he spent his first six seasons. That game was supposed to be Jones's revenge game. Instead he'll be watching it from waivers.

Jones is 29. He signed that two-year deal in March, with $50 million fully guaranteed — $100 million with incentives, the largest two-year contract in NFL history, per the New York Post. The Colts paid $49.79 million, per Over The Cap via the Post.

The final game

Thursday night in Houston was the end of it, even if nobody said so at the time. The Texans beat the Colts 26-3, and Jones went 12-of-27 for 144 yards with an interception before Steichen pulled him in the fourth quarter for Richardson, who went 0-for-2 with one carry for two yards.

Steichen was noncommittal about Jones's job after the loss. By Friday, there was no job to be noncommittal about.

The season line tells the story on its own: a 3-8 record, 1,974 passing yards, 7 touchdowns and 13 interceptions — the most interceptions in the league and a career high for Jones — with a career-low 58.4 percent completion rate.

Why now

The timing is about money as much as football. Jones carried a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 that would have become fully guaranteed if he got hurt, so a benching was coming either way. The Colts skipped the benching and went straight to the release.

Jones was set to be a $46.8 million cap hit next season. The release saves Indianapolis about $11.6 million, with dead cap of $14,889,520 in 2026 and $35,200,000 in 2027, per Spotrac via USA Today.

The deadline blunder

The part that will sting in Indianapolis is what happened 10 days ago. Baltimore and Minnesota were both interested in trading for Jones at the deadline, and the Colts kept him off the market. Now they get nothing for him. He is on waivers through Monday at 4 p.m.

A team that wanted him at the deadline can now have him for the cost of a waiver claim. That is the whole story of this Colts season in one paragraph.

The backstory

This is the second time in three years that Jones has been released in November. The first was the Giants in 2024 — but that time, he sought it. This time, Indianapolis made the call.

It is a strange ending to a stint that started so well. Jones's Colts run opened 8-2 in 2025 before a torn Achilles cut his season short. He tried to play last season on a broken leg until the Achilles snapped — the kind of toughness that made Steichen's praise on Friday land as more than a courtesy.

"Can't say enough good things about Daniel, just the ultimate competitor, ultimate teammate, toughness that he brought to the football team," Steichen said.

And on the release itself, Steichen was blunt about who made the decision: "No. This was a decision that was just made for the best interest of both parties." Jones did not ask for the release. "It's just where we're at in our season," Steichen said.

What it means

Their general manager Chris Ballard was fired on October 19, and they already moved captains Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner at the deadline. This is a teardown, and Jones was the most expensive piece left to move.

For Richardson, it is a second chance that nobody saw coming a month ago. His first one back is against the Giants — the same franchise Jones was supposed to face with a point to prove. The revenge game still happens. It just has a different quarterback, and a different kind of point to prove.

Up next: the Colts host the Giants on Sunday, November 29.

Montgomery took the whole Texans backfield

By Matt

David Montgomery returned from a four-game groin absence and carried 26 times for 107 yards as the Texans rolled the Colts 26-3 — Houston's first 100-yard rusher of the season.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

David Montgomery didn't ease back in. Returning Thursday night after four games out with a groin injury, the Houston Texans running back carried 26 times for 107 yards in a 26-3 rout of the Indianapolis Colts — season highs in both categories, and the first time any Texan has topped 100 rushing yards this season.

There was no ramp-up plan. With starter Woody Marks inactive after suffering a concussion last week, Montgomery took the backfield outright from the opening drive and never gave it back, finishing with 29 touches and 124 yards from scrimmage.

The backfield split

Houston leaned on the run all night, and the split tells the story of who owned it:

David Montgomery: 26; 107; 3; 17; 29

Emari Demercado: 5; 33; 2; -4; 7

Montgomery's 70% share of the team's rushing attempts was the heaviest single-game workload of his season, and the most carries he's logged in a game since Week 4 of 2023. Demercado, claimed off waivers from Dallas last month, handled the change-of-pace role — and that was it. Nobody else in the backfield touched the ball.

The efficiency matched the volume. Montgomery averaged 4.1 yards per carry with a long of 15, and per NFL Next Gen Stats, about 92% of his yardage came inside the tackles — steady, grinding runs that kept the chains moving and the clock running. His workload only grew in the fourth quarter as Houston bled the clock rather than chasing more points.

Why it matters

This was the ground game Houston had been missing all season. The Texans hadn't produced a 100-yard rusher in ten weeks, and the 167 team rushing yards against Indianapolis were their best of the year. Montgomery's return gave C.J. Stroud the balance the offense had lacked since Week 5 — Stroud threw three touchdowns (to Nico Collins, Kayshon Boutte, and rookie Marlin Klein for his first NFL score) on a night he only needed 194 passing yards.

The performance also marked just the third time since 2024 that Montgomery has topped 120 yards from scrimmage, and his best outing since a Week 1 hat trick against the Buffalo Bills. For a back who arrived in Houston as a veteran addition, it was the first game that looked like the role the Texans signed him for.

The test gets harder fast. Houston travels to Baltimore next weekend to face a Ravens defense that has been solid against the run all season, and Marks' return would split the work again. But for one night, the backfield belonged to one man — and the Texans finally looked like a team that can run the ball.

Berkly Catton's first career hat trick powers the Kraken past the Canucks 5-1

By Matt

Berkly Catton scored in every period — a power-play one-timer, a steal-and-score, and an empty-netter — for his first career NHL hat trick as the Kraken beat the Canucks 5-1.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Berkly Catton scored his first career NHL hat trick — a goal in every period — as the Seattle Kraken beat the Vancouver Canucks 5-1 at Climate Pledge Arena on Thursday night, snapping a three-game losing streak in their first game back from the Global Series trip to Helsinki.

Catton opened the scoring on the power play at 7:37 of the first, one-timing a Brandon Montour feed from the right dot over Leevi Merilainen's glove. He made it 3-1 at 8:54 of the second, stealing the puck from Linus Karlsson in the neutral zone and scoring unassisted, 54 seconds after Matty Beniers had restored the lead. And he completed it with 43 seconds left, taking a pass from Freddy Gaudreau — who passed up the easy empty-netter himself to set up the milestone — and snapping it home for the 5-1 final.

Catton finished with three goals on four shots in 15:17 of ice time. At 20 years and 310 days old, he is the youngest player in Kraken history to record a hat trick, eclipsing Jared McCann, who was 26 years and 228 days when he did it on January 14, 2023. Catton is the fifth Kraken player ever with a hat trick, joining Jordan Eberle, McCann, Montour and Jaden Schwartz.

The season he's having

The hat trick pushed Catton to eight goals on the season — already past the seven he scored in 66 games as a rookie last year — with 17 points in 19 games. He's on pace for 35 goals.

That pace is the story now. A year ago he was a rookie finding his way; this season he's the Kraken's breakout, scoring in every kind of situation — power play, off a steal, into an empty net — and doing it on a night when Seattle needed a response after a difficult trip to Finland.

The game around him

Seattle overwhelmed Vancouver from the opening faceoff, finishing with 43 shots on goal — tied for the fifth-highest single-game total in franchise history — including 24 in the first period alone, a franchise record for one period. Beniers had a goal and an assist, with his second-period goal standing as the game-winner, and Jordan Eberle scored on the power play in the third, four points away from 800 for his career. Montour had two assists. Philipp Grubauer made 22 saves.

Jake DeBrusk scored Vancouver's only goal, on the power play in the first period, with an assist from Brock Boeser that extended Boeser's point streak to nine games.

What it means

A first hat trick is a milestone by itself. Doing it as the youngest in franchise history, in the first game back from Helsinki, while snapping a losing streak, makes it a statement. Catton isn't just having a good sophomore season — he's becoming the player the Kraken build around.

Up next: the Kraken host the Sharks on Saturday, November 21 at 10:00 PM ET.

Sports · Nov 20, 2026 · 9:30 AM ET

Scott Wedgewood's 25-save shutout blanks the Ducks as the Avalanche end Cutter Gauthier's 10-game goal streak

By Matt

Scott Wedgewood stopped all 25 shots for his first shutout of the season as the Avalanche beat the Ducks 4-0 in Denver — and ended Cutter Gauthier's 10-game goal streak.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Scott Wedgewood made 25 saves for his first shutout of the season as the Colorado Avalanche beat the Anaheim Ducks 4-0 at Ball Arena on Thursday night. It was the 13th shutout of Wedgewood's career, and his seventh as a member of the Avalanche.

The shutout ended the story of the NHL season so far. Cutter Gauthier came into Denver on a 10-game goal streak — four hat tricks in November, 19 goals across the streak, three shy of the NHL record for goals in a calendar month — and Wedgewood stopped him cold. The Ducks rang two shots off the post and kept coming, but nothing got through.

"I think it's hard not to see it. He's on every Instagram page and every media highlight right now. I skated with him this summer," Wedgewood said of Gauthier after the game.

The game around him

Colorado broke it open in the second period. Nicolas Roy scored eight seconds into the middle frame, Brock Nelson added a power-play goal at 3:25 and another at 10:04, and Devon Toews made it 4-0 at 10:33 of the third on a give-and-go with Nelson. Nelson finished with two goals and an assist, Toews had a goal and an assist, and Martin Necas set up two. Lukas Dostal made 23 saves for Anaheim.

The shutout stretched a quieter streak, too: Colorado has now gone 165:25 without allowing a regulation home goal, dating back to November 5 against Nashville.

The Avalanche improve to 13-7-3 and have won four of their past six. The Ducks fall to 11-11-1 and have lost four of five.

What it means

A shutout is a shutout, but this one lands harder because of who was on the other side. Gauthier's streak was the hottest run in hockey — the kind of thing that had the whole league watching every Ducks game — and Wedgewood ended it with a clean sheet on home ice. Colorado didn't just beat Anaheim; it took away the one thing everyone tuned in to see.

Gauthier's November still stands at 19 goals, three short of the calendar-month record shared by Teemu Selanne (March 1993) and Joe Malone (February 1921). He'll get another crack at it — but the streak itself is over.

Up next: the Avalanche host the Canadiens on Wednesday, November 25 at 9:30 PM ET.

Travis Konecny caps a four-point night with an OT winner as the Flyers rally from three down to stun the Senators 6-5

By Matt

Travis Konecny scored 39 seconds into overtime to cap a four-point night as the Flyers erased a 5-2 third-period deficit and beat the Senators 6-5 in Ottawa.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Travis Konecny scored 39 seconds into overtime to finish a four-point night as the Philadelphia Flyers rallied from three goals down in the third period to beat the Ottawa Senators 6-5 at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday night.

Konecny came into the game with two goals, four assists and six points in 14 games — a slow start by his standards. He left it having factored into four of Philadelphia's six goals, including the winner. He assisted on Owen Tippett's first-period power-play goal, set up Cam York's late second-period goal that cut the deficit to 3-2, fed Tyson Foerster on a 2-on-1 in the third, and then ended it himself, racing up the left wing and wiring a shot from the circle that squeezed past former Flyers goaltender Samuel Ersson.

It was Konecny's fourth career overtime goal, tied for the eighth-most in Flyers history. Claude Giroux leads the list with 11.

The comeback

The Flyers were dead in the water six minutes into the third period, trailing 5-2. Then York swatted in a bouncing puck to make it 5-3, and fifteen seconds later Konecny fed Foerster to bring it within one. With goaltender Joseph Woll pulled during 4-on-4 play, Jamie Drysdale walked in from the blue line and snapped a shot past Ersson at 17:27 of the third — 2:33 left — to tie it 5-5 and force overtime.

Four unanswered goals, all in the third period and overtime. It was the seventh third-period, three-goal comeback victory in Flyers history, and the first since they beat the Buffalo Sabres 4-3 in overtime on March 29, 2021.

York finished with two goals, Foerster had a goal and an assist, and Drysdale had a goal and two assists. Woll made 21 saves — and picked up an assist on Konecny's overtime winner, his first of the season and the second point of his career.

The game around him

Ottawa got two goals from Dylan Cozens and two assists from Tim Stutzle, and Claude Giroux scored against his former team early. But the Senators couldn't hold a three-goal lead at home, and the Flyers — who have now won two straight and are 4-1-1 in their past six — stole two points in a building where they looked finished with 14 minutes to play.

Philadelphia improves to 8-11-6.

What it means

This is the Konecny the Flyers have been waiting on. The first 14 games were quiet for a player who is supposed to drive this team, and one night doesn't erase that — but a four-point game capped by an overtime winner, with his fingerprints on every part of the comeback, is the kind of performance that turns a season around. If this is the version of Konecny that shows up the rest of the way, the Flyers' record starts moving.

Up next: the Flyers visit the Canadiens in Montreal on Saturday, November 21 at 7:00 PM ET.

NHL · Nov 20, 2026 · 9:09 AM ET

McDavid's 23-game point streak ends in Tampa

By Matt

Tampa Bay held Connor McDavid off the scoresheet for the first time all season, ending his 23-game point streak — tied with Wayne Gretzky for the fourth-longest in NHL history — in a 3-1 Lightning win.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Connor McDavid's season-opening point streak is over. The Tampa Bay Lightning held the Edmonton Oilers captain without a goal or an assist for the first time all season, ending the run at 23 games in a 3-1 win on Thursday night at Benchmark International Arena.

The run produced 55 points — 13 goals and 42 assists — and McDavid still leads the NHL in scoring. But Tampa became the first team this season to keep him off the scoresheet, and the Oilers' six-game winning streak went down with it.

How Tampa shut him down

The Lightning matched their checking line against McDavid all night. Anthony Cirelli centered a line with Ilya Mikheyev and Pontus Holmberg, and the trio held the league's scoring leader to two shots on goal in 22:57 of ice time.

Edmonton actually controlled the early going, outshooting Tampa 7-3 in a scoreless first period. The Lightning's penalty kill handled Edmonton's first two power plays, then the home side struck on its own man advantage late in the second: Brayden Point fed Jake Guentzel below the goal line, Guentzel worked around the net, and John Carlson's one-timer found the top corner with 6:31 left in the period.

Mikheyev made it 2-0 at 10:46 of the third, burying the rebound after Erik Cernak's initial chance was stopped. Nikita Kucherov added a breakaway goal less than four minutes later to make it 3-0. Colton Dach spoiled Andrei Vasilevskiy's shutout bid with 1:36 left, but that was all Edmonton could manage.

John Carlson (TBL, PP): 2nd, 13:29; TBL 1-0

Ilya Mikheyev (TBL): 3rd, 10:46; TBL 2-0

Nikita Kucherov (TBL): 3rd, 14:29; TBL 3-0

Colton Dach (EDM): 3rd, 18:24; TBL 3-1

Vasilevskiy stopped 23 of 24 shots. Levi made 17 saves for Edmonton, which went 0-for-3 on the power play and lost in regulation on the road for the first time this season (10-1-1).

Where the run sits in history

The streak ends tied with Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 run for the fourth-longest point streak in NHL history. The only longer ones belong to Gretzky's 51-game run in 1983-84 — the record — and the two runs between it and this one. McDavid needed seven more games to reach the next spot on the list.

What made it stand out wasn't just the length. It was a season-opening streak: McDavid had a point in every game Edmonton played, from opening night through mid-November, while the Oilers built a 17-4-3 record and the league's best road mark. Tampa didn't just end the streak — it handed Edmonton its first regulation road loss and snapped a six-game winning streak in the same night.

The Lightning, meanwhile, keep rolling at home. The win moved Tampa to 15-5-2 overall and 10-1-0 at Benchmark International Arena, with four wins in its past five games.

Edmonton gets a quick chance to start a new one: the Oilers open a weekend back-to-back Saturday afternoon against the Carolina Hurricanes.

Gaming · Nov 20, 2026 · 3:08 AM ET

GTA VI sold 24.58 million copies by Thursday evening

By Matt

Grand Theft Auto VI moved an estimated 24.58 million copies worth about $2.36 billion by the end of launch day, nearly triple GTA V's first-day haul — and the world watched along with it.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on November 19, 2026, after 13 years of waiting — and by Thursday evening it had sold an estimated 24.58 million copies, worth about $2.36 billion. The launch didn't just break the old record. It nearly tripled it.

Launch day by the numbers

Copies sold by Thursday evening: 24.58 million (est.)

Estimated revenue: $2.36 billion

Peak simultaneous viewers: 7.91 million

Hours watched in first 24 hours: 125.47 million

PlayStation 5 share: ~75% (18.44 million copies, $1.77 billion)

Xbox Series X\: S share; ~25% (6.15 million copies, $588 million)

The numbers come from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, as reported by Reuters, GameSpot, and Deadline. One caveat matters: none of this is official yet. Take-Two Interactive has not released its own sales figures, and chief executive Strauss Zelnick has said official data will be shared soon. Until then, every figure here is a third-party estimate — but it is an estimate built on store data, and it moved in one direction all week.

How the total climbed

The tracker told the story in real time. Pre-orders alone crossed $1 billion from an estimated 10.31 million units eight days before release, and by midday Wednesday — before the game had even unlocked — the running estimate stood at 17.1 million copies and $1.65 billion. Thursday morning it was 19.1 million and $1.84 billion. Then launch day did the rest, adding roughly $520 million between the morning and evening snapshots.

Pre-order revenue passed $2 billion through launch day, which made the game 2026's best-selling title on pre-orders alone before a single copy was played. Sensor Tower's Karl Kontus put it plainly: the game "has captivated consumers, becoming 2026's best-selling game based on pre-orders alone."

Against the old record

The comparison that frames the scale is GTA V. The previous game earned roughly $800 million in its first 24 hours in September 2013, on 11.21 million copies — a mark Guinness World Records recognizes as the best single-day haul for any video game. It needed three days to pass $1 billion.

The new game cleared that bar before most players had finished downloading it. The estimated day-one revenue is nearly three times the old figure, and the unit count is more than double. The old record stood for 13 years. The new one arrived in a single evening.

Leonida, finally open

The game itself is set in Leonida, a fictional Florida, with Vice City at its center. Lucia and Jason — the dual protagonists introduced across the trailers — anchor a story 13 years in the making, and the launch finally puts the state players have been dissecting frame by frame since the first trailer in December 2023 into their hands.

It is out now on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There is no PC version yet.

The world watched, too

The launch was a viewing event as much as a sales event. The game peaked at 7.91 million simultaneous viewers, with 125.47 million hours watched in the first 24 hours — launch-day streams, first playthroughs, and reaction content running around the clock. The sales record and the viewership record arrived together, which is fitting: for a game this anticipated, watching it was half the launch.

Sources: GTA 6 passes $2.36 billion in estimated launch-day sales · GTA 6 day one sales estimates break 24.5 million with $2.36 billion earned · GTA 6 sold an estimated 24.6 million copies worth about $2.36 billion on its first day, Sensor Tower says

MLB · Nov 19, 2026 · 9:10 PM ET

Duran tops Boston's Friday non-tender board

By Matt

Jarren Duran's $11.1 million projected salary and crowded outfield make him Boston's biggest non-tender decision before Friday's 5 p.m. deadline.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The Red Sox have until Friday at 5 p.m. ET to decide whether Jarren Duran is still one of theirs. MLB's contract tender deadline hits then, and Boston has to tender contracts to every unsigned player on its 40-man roster or watch them become free agents immediately. Duran, the 2024 All-Star Game MVP, is the name at the top of the board — and a trade looks likelier than a straight non-tender.

The deadline

The mechanics are simple: tender a contract and the player stays under team control, with the two sides free to keep negotiating until an arbitration hearing. Don't tender, and the player hits the open market the same day. Duran is arbitration-eligible for 2027 and 2028, so the decision isn't just about next season — it's about whether Boston wants to pay a projected $11.1 million (via MLB Trade Rumors) for a player who no longer has a clear everyday role.

He isn't the only name on Boston's list. First baseman Triston Casas is among the other potential cuts, per NBC Sports Boston, but Duran is the one with real trade value still attached.

The case against paying him

Duran's 2026 season was the worst of his career, and it wasn't close. The full line:

Games: 151

Average: .207

On-base: .266

Slugging: .361

OPS: .627

Home runs: 20

Stolen bases: 21

RBI: 69

Strikeouts: 165

Walks: 41

wRC+: 69

That wRC+ — 31 percent below league average — was the second-worst mark among qualified hitters in baseball, per MLB Trade Rumors. The strikeout rate climbed to 27.1 percent, up from 24.3 percent in 2025 and 21.8 percent in his breakout year. The one thing that didn't crater was the power-speed combination: he still reached 20 homers and 21 steals, the second 20-20 season of his career, which is what makes him a change-of-scenery candidate rather than a straight release.

From All-Star MVP to the bubble

The fall is what makes this one sting. Two years ago Duran was one of the best players in baseball: a .285/.342/.492 line in 2024, an All-Star selection, and the Ted Williams Award as All-Star Game MVP after a tiebreaking two-run homer off Hunter Greene lifted the American League to a 5-3 win. He led the majors in doubles (48) and triples (14), stole 34 bases, and finished eighth in AL MVP voting. He followed that with a 4.0 fWAR season in 2025 — a step back, but still a useful everyday player.

Then came the collapse. The extra-base hits dried up — 15 doubles and five triples after 62 combined in 2024 — and the strikeouts piled up. Boston's outfield, meanwhile, got younger and more settled around him: Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu are the projected starters, and the club just signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal to be the primary designated hitter. With Bauers at DH, Duran and Masataka Yoshida — due $18.6 million next season — are left fighting for bench at-bats at starter money.

The trade market

Boston has been shopping Duran since the GM Meetings, and the interest is real even at his lowest value. The San Diego Padres have long admired him and are doing background work again. The Seattle Mariners and Philadelphia Phillies have each poked around, per MassLive's Chris Cotillo. The Chicago Cubs evaluated him as a potential change-of-scenery addition this week, The Athletic's Patrick Mooney reported Thursday, and the Cubs are also in on posted Japanese outfielder Teruaki Sato.

The leverage is thin. Boston's own reporting has it that the Red Sox don't want to pay $11.1 million in arbitration for a player who is, at best, a fourth outfielder — USA Today's Bob Nightengale put it bluntly: "He should be as good as gone." But letting him walk for nothing would sting for a front office already criticized for not trading him when his value peaked after 2024. A trade, even for a modest return, beats a non-tender.

What happens Friday

If no deal materializes by 5 p.m., Boston faces a straight choice: tender him and swallow the arbitration number, or non-tender him and let the market set his price — almost certainly well below $11.1 million. Either way, it would be a surprise to see Duran back in a Red Sox uniform in 2027. The deadline forces the answer.
