Golden Chocobo bids $85,400 at Goldin

By Matt

A PSA 8 serialized Golden Traveling Chocobo — #71 of just 77 ever printed — is bidding at $85,400 in Goldin's fall TCG auction, days after a sibling copy reportedly changed hands for $1.4 million.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The golden bird is back on the block. A PSA 8 serialized Golden Traveling Chocobo — card #71 of the entire print run — is bidding at $85,400 with buyer's premium in Goldin's 2026 Fall TCG Elite Auction, and the auction is still live.

The card

This is the 2025 Magic: The Gathering — Final Fantasy serialized Golden Chocobo (#0551f Traveling Chocobo), the gold-foiled chase card from the set. Wizards printed the serialized version in English Collector Boosters only, each copy stamped with its own number, and the odds of pulling one were under 0.1% per pack, according to CGC. ICv2 calls it one of the scarcest Magic cards in existence, and it rarely shows up at auction at all.

It's also not clear how many of the print run ever made it into collectors' hands — the rest could still be sitting in sealed product. Unopened Collector Boosters for the set are going for roughly $1,500 a box.

The timing is the story

This listing lands days after a sibling copy made headlines of its own. Copy #47 — a PSA Gem Mint 10 that also carries an MBA Gold Diamond evaluation — was reported sold in a private deal for $1.4 million, per MTG Rocks and Draftsim on November 17. The seller was named as Adam Cai, also known as Pristine_Collectibles, with the report traced to Collectr.

A note of caution on that figure: it is a reported private sale, not an auction result. No buyer identity, settlement document, or payment record has been published, and one extraordinary sale does not set a market price for the rest of the print run. The previous confirmed record for the card was $250,000 — less than a fifth of the reported number.

Recent auction comps put the Goldin bid in context. A CGC 8 copy realized $75,000 at Fanatics Collect in March, and another CGC 8 went for $67,100 at Goldin in September 2025. Draftsim notes most copies known to have changed hands have sold in the $40,000–$80,000 range, which is exactly where this listing sits right now.

The rest of the auction

Goldin's fall sale is stacked beyond the Chocobo. The current headline lots include:

Illustrator Pikachu: $488,000

1st Edition Base Set box: $231,800

Final Fantasy Collector Boosters (unopened): ~$1,500

The Chocobo is the Magic headliner, but the Pikachu is the auction's top lot by a wide margin.

Sports · Nov 19, 2026 · 12:23 PM ET

Jalen Johnson's second triple-double in five days powers Hawks past Thunder 117-112

By Matt

Jalen Johnson put up 16 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists — his second triple-double in five days — as the Hawks beat the Thunder 117-112 in Oklahoma City.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Jalen Johnson recorded a triple-double with 16 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists as the Atlanta Hawks beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 117-112 on Wednesday night at Paycom Center. It was his second triple-double in five days — he put up 27 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists at Chicago on November 13 — and it handed the Thunder their first home loss of the season.

Both teams now sit at 9-6, but the night belonged to Atlanta's balance. Onyeka Okongwu led the Hawks with 28 points and nine rebounds, Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 19 points and seven assists, and Dyson Daniels chipped in 10 points and 10 rebounds. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led all scorers with 34 for Oklahoma City, and Jared McCain added 18 off the bench.

The homecoming stole the first half of the story

The game was circled on the calendar the moment the schedule came out: Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins were back in Oklahoma City for the first time since being traded to Atlanta this past offseason. Both helped the Thunder win the 2024-25 NBA championship, and the home crowd gave them standing ovations and video tributes — Wiggins during the first media timeout, Dort after the first quarter.

They made sure the return was more than a ceremony. Dort finished with 16 points, three rebounds and two steals, knocking down three triples. Wiggins scored 14. And when the game swung in the fourth quarter, it was the two former Thunder players who swung it.

How it played out

Oklahoma City erased a 13-point halftime deficit to tie the game at 83 entering the fourth quarter. Then, in the first 1:15 of the final frame — with Gilgeous-Alexander on the bench — Atlanta retook control with three straight three-pointers: Wiggins, then Dort, then Wiggins again. The Hawks never gave the lead back, winning the fourth 34-29.

Atlanta's shooting carried the night. The Hawks hit 20 of 50 from three-point range and outrebounded the Thunder 50-43, while Oklahoma City went 9 of 26 from deep. Gilgeous-Alexander got his 34, but he missed critical late shots as the comeback fell short, including a mid-range jumper off the front of the rim and a pull-up three in the final seconds.

Johnson is stacking them now

Five days ago in Chicago, Johnson's triple-double came in an overtime win. This one came on the road against the defending champions' building, with the game still in the balance. The 16 points were the quietest part of the line — the 12 rebounds and 11 assists were the engine, with Atlanta's ball movement and second chances built around his playmaking.

The Hawks have now won back-to-back games and six of their last eight. The Thunder have dropped four of their last five.

NHL · Nov 19, 2026 · 9:08 AM ET

Bruins end skid with 4-1 win in Detroit

By Matt

Four unanswered goals, a Pavel Zacha power-play winner and a three-game skid snapped — Boston beats Detroit 4-1 on the 100th anniversary of the Red Wings' first NHL game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The Boston Bruins snapped their three-game losing streak the hard way — falling behind early in Detroit, then answering with four unanswered goals to beat the Red Wings 4-1 on Wednesday night at Little Caesars Arena.

It was a fitting stage for a bounce-back. The game landed exactly 100 years to the day after Detroit's first NHL game, a 2-0 loss for the then-Cougars to the Bruins at Border Cities Arena in Windsor, Ontario. A century later, Boston spoiled the centennial night the same way.

How it played out

Lucas Raymond put Detroit in front late in the first period, finishing a 2-on-1 rush with a one-timer at 16:58. Boston answered early in the second, when JJ Peterka kept the puck on a 2-on-1 of his own and beat Daniil Tarasov over the glove to tie it at 2:49.

The turning point came on the power play. Pavel Zacha buried a net-front rebound at 11:48 of the second to give Boston its first lead, and the Bruins never gave it back. David Pastrnak added insurance at 5:11 of the third, taking a drop pass from Mason Lohrei on a rush, cutting into the slot and beating Tarasov glove side. Casey Mittelstadt sealed it with an empty-net goal at 19:05.

Lucas Raymond (DET): 1st, 16:58; DET 1-0

JJ Peterka (BOS): 2nd, 2:49; 1-1

Pavel Zacha (BOS, PP): 2nd, 11:48; BOS 2-1

David Pastrnak (BOS): 3rd, 5:11; BOS 3-1

Casey Mittelstadt (BOS, EN): 3rd, 19:05; BOS 4-1

The top line delivered — and so did the depth

Pastrnak, Zacha and Mittelstadt each finished with a goal and an assist, and the scoring was spread across the lineup: four different Bruins found the net, and six players recorded a point. Morgan Geekie and Lohrei each picked up two assists, with Lohrei setting up both the tying goal and Pastrnak's insurance marker.

Pastrnak's goal was his 10th of the season. With the two points he now leads Boston in goals, assists (18) and points (28). Zacha's winner was his sixth goal of the year, and he sits at 17 points.

In net, Jeremy Swayman stopped 20 of 21 shots for his 10th win of the season. Tarasov made 27 saves for Detroit. Boston also did the dirty work in front of its goalie, blocking 23 shots.

Why this one mattered

Three straight losses had put the Bruins in a corner, and the response was a complete road game: a comeback from an early deficit, a power play that converted on its only chance, and a third period that stayed locked down until the empty-netter. Detroit, meanwhile, has now lost six of its past seven despite coming off a 2-0 win at Tampa Bay on Saturday.

Boston (14-7-1) returns home to TD Garden to host the Washington Capitals on Saturday night. Detroit falls to 8-11-3.

Gaming · Nov 19, 2026 · 3:08 AM ET

Ludwig starts a GTA VI marathon on launch day

By Matt

Ludwig kicks off a GTA VI marathon at 3 p.m. ET on launch day, streaming non-stop until the game is finished — at his own pace, with a code for viewers every hour on the hour.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Ludwig is spending launch day the way only he would: live, non-stop, and in no hurry. The streamer kicks off a Grand Theft Auto VI marathon at 3 p.m. ET on Thursday, November 19 — the day the game launches — and the stream does not end until the game is done.

Taking his time

The hook here is the pace. Ludwig has been running marathon streams for five years, and he says he has noticed a pattern lately: streamers speed through a game to beat it as fast as possible, and he has been guilty of it himself. His verdict is that rushing cheapens the experience — so for GTA VI, he is taking his time.

The plan was announced by his company, Mogul Moves, on Monday, November 16 at 8:00 p.m. ET: "Ludwig's GTA VI Marathon starts Thursday, November 19." The same post added the one-line rule for the run: "Stream doesn't end until the game is done." About an hour later, Ludwig quoted the announcement with his thinking in full:

> "i have been marathoning games on stream for 5 years and ive noticed a trend recently where it feels like people speed through the game to try to beat it as quickly as possible"

>

> "ive been guilty of this as well and i realized it cheapens the experience"

>

> "so for GTA VI im TAKING MY TIME"

A viewer then asked for an exact start time, and Ludwig replied it "should start at noon PT" — 3 p.m. ET.

The hourly code

There is a reason to keep the stream open even when he is wandering Vice City instead of pushing the story. Ludwig is giving out a code for viewers every hour on the hour for the entire marathon. His stream recap describes the giveaway as game codes, handed out hourly across a run expected to last around 60 hours — though the announcement itself does not say what the code is for, and no platform was named in the post.

Launch day is a marathon for everyone

Ludwig is not the only big name clearing the calendar. The launch has turned into a streaming event of its own:

Kai Cenat: Full playthrough from 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, November 18, on YouTube and Twitch

IShowSpeed: Starts 9 p.m. ET Wednesday, November 18, in 10- to 12-hour days — no marathon

Ludwig: Non-stop from 3 p.m. ET Thursday, November 19, at a relaxed pace

YouTube: 24-hour launch livestream from midnight ET November 19, with an RDCWorld pre-show at 11 p.m. ET November 18

The contrast is the story: Cenat goes first and goes all-in, Speed deliberately paces himself across days, and Ludwig splits the difference — non-stop, but refusing to race. In a launch week where being first to the credits is the default flex, the streamer who built his name on endurance broadcasts is betting that slowing down is the better show.

Blackhawks beat Maple Leafs 6-3 on centennial night — Bertuzzi and Nazar each score twice, 100 years to the day after the franchise's first NHL game

By Matt

Tyler Bertuzzi scored twice against his former club and Frank Nazar added two of his own as the Blackhawks beat the Maple Leafs 6-3 on the 100th anniversary of the franchise's first NHL game — a win that came at a cost, with Connor Bedard leaving early in the third period with an apparent shoulder injury.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

One hundred years to the day after the Black Hawks beat the Toronto St. Patricks 4-1 in their first NHL game, the Chicago Blackhawks beat the same franchise again — 6-3 over the Toronto Maple Leafs at the United Center on Tuesday night, November 17, 2026, on the franchise's centennial night.

Tyler Bertuzzi scored twice and added an assist against his former club, and Frank Nazar scored twice of his own. The six goals were the most Chicago has scored in a single game this season, and they came in a rush — all six in about 26 minutes of game time, including three in a span of 3:03 in the third period.

How it unfolded

Toronto struck first. Easton Cowan put the Leafs up 1-0 at 3:22 of the opening period, and the game stayed quiet until late in the second.

Nazar tied it on the power play at 13:17 of the second, walking in and ripping a wrist shot past Sergei Bobrovsky. He struck again at 17:54, taking Cole Smith's feed at the blue line, driving down the right side and beating Bobrovsky from the right dot for a 2-1 lead. It was his ninth and 10th goals of the season, and his fifth in three games — he now leads the team in goals.

Teddy Blueger tied it 22 seconds later, at 18:16. Bedard answered 35 seconds after that, at 18:51, snapping a wrist shot home off a feed from Bertuzzi to make it 3-2 after two. It was his seventh goal of the season.

Bertuzzi put Chicago up 4-2 with a power-play goal at 9:07 of the third, banking in a Sam Rinzel setup. After John Tavares pulled Toronto within one, Bertuzzi and Oliver Moore answered in the flurry — Bertuzzi's second of the night came at 12:10, cleaning up in front after Frondell's attempt was stopped, for the 6-3 final.

Rinzel finished with three assists. Bobrovsky made 19 saves on 25 shots for Toronto.

The cost

The win came with a scare. Bedard left the game 54 seconds into the third period with an apparent upper-body injury suffered while taking a faceoff, and did not return. Coach Jeff Blashill said after the game that Bedard would undergo more testing. It looked like a re-injury of the same right shoulder Bedard hurt last December, which cost him nearly a month.

The context

A century is a long time to wait for a sequel, and the symmetry was exact: the Blackhawks' first NHL game came against the Toronto St. Patricks at the Chicago Coliseum on November 17, 1926 — a 4-1 win. One hundred years later, against the same franchise, they won again, on the same date, in front of a home crowd celebrating the milestone.

For Toronto, the loss was the seventh straight — a skid that has dropped the Leafs to last in the Atlantic Division. For Chicago, the win moved the club to 2-0-1 on its four-game homestand, with Columbus coming to the United Center on Thursday night.

What it means

Centennial nights can go either way — a ceremony that swallows the game, or a game that lives up to the ceremony. This one did the latter. Nazar is now the team's goal leader, Bertuzzi beat his old team twice in one night, and the Hawks put up their biggest offensive night of the season. The only thing that matters now is Bedard's shoulder.

GTA 6 launches at midnight tonight — Vice City is open, and our Vice City tee is ready for launch night

By Matt

Grand Theft Auto VI unlocks at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S — and the Vice City T-Shirt is built for the night we've all been waiting for.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Tonight's the night

Grand Theft Auto VI unlocks at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. On the West Coast, that means 9 p.m. PT tonight — Rockstar confirmed the timing to the USA Today Network — so the wait ends before the calendar even flips for a lot of players.

This is the return to Vice City, in the state of Leonida, with two leads — Lucia and Jason — at the center of it. The launch trailer, released October 15 and captured entirely in-game on PS5, is built around the pair: Jason talking about leaving the army on bad terms, the two of them in armed set pieces all over Vice City, scored by Justice's "Flower in a Hurricane" featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. It has pulled roughly 80 million views since it dropped.

What to know before midnight

The standard edition runs $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition $99.99, with the same November 19 date for both — there is no paid early-access window. There is no PC version at launch, and Rockstar has not announced a PC date. The install needs up to 212 GB of space, so clear room now if you haven't. The physical release is a code-in-box package with no disc inside. Buy before November 20 and the purchase includes the Vintage Vice City Pack.

Pre-loading has been open since November 10, so anyone who pre-ordered digitally should already be sitting on the download. If you're planning to watch instead of play, YouTube and Rockstar are running a 24-hour GTA VI livestream starting at midnight ET on launch day, with an RDCWorld pre-show at 11 p.m. ET tonight.

The wait is over

This one has been more than a decade in the making since GTA V, and the demand has matched the wait. Sensor Tower estimates about 12.1 million digital pre-orders worth roughly $1.18 billion before a single copy reaches a shelf, and Sony and Microsoft have both confirmed it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of their storefronts. It also arrives as the most-nominated game at The Game Awards 2026, with eight nominations including Game of the Year — two days before it even launches.

Launch-night gear: the Vice City tee

We made something for tonight. The Vice City T-Shirt ($30) is our original GTA 6 launch design — a glowing sun disc over a lit Vice City skyline, zero text, zero logos, just the vibe. It's in the TSL shop now, and it's the shirt to wear while the city loads in.

If you still need the game itself, GTA VI for PlayStation 5 is on Amazon. And if your setup needs a last-minute upgrade before midnight, Razer is where we look first.

ARC Raiders 2.6 brings back Cold Snap

By Matt

Embark Studios launched Live Update 2.6.0 on November 17, bringing Cold Snap back to the map rotation, a new Outlaw Weapon Stencil Set, a 50% Black Friday discount, and a first look at Flickering Flames Part 1 arriving November 24.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Embark Studios launched Live Update 2.6.0 for ARC Raiders on November 17, 2026. The headline is the return of Cold Snap to the Major Map Condition rotation, just as the snow settles in — and the update pairs it with a new weapon stencil set, a long list of fixes, a 50% Black Friday discount, and a first look at the Flickering Flames project arriving November 24.

Cold Snap is back

Cold Snap rejoins the Major Map Condition rotation in 2.6.0. Embark's own note on it is short — "As the days get colder and snow settles in, Cold Snap is back!" — but the condition changes how every run plays: snow, reduced visibility, and the cold itself become part of the extraction, on top of the ARC machines and rival Raiders already competing for the same loot.

It is a return, not a debut. Cold Snap first arrived as the game's winter update in December 2025, and its comeback a year later lands alongside a fresh event built around the same season.

What's new in 2.6.0

Cold Snap: Back in the Major Map Condition rotation

Outlaw Weapon Stencil Set: Three weapon stencils — Taurus, Sundob, and Malocchio — now in the in-game store rotation

Buried items: The Dockmaster's Detector now finds buried items on all maps except Pendola Pass (which still needs the Mountaineer's Detector); the Beachcombing minor condition is gone from Riven Tides

50% discount: Black Friday sale on the base game and Deluxe Edition, dates vary by platform (below)

The buried-items change is the quiet quality-of-life win in the patch. What used to be a Riven Tides-only mechanic is now available almost everywhere, so detector runs are worth doing no matter which map the rotation serves up.

The 50% Black Friday sale

New players can join topside at half price, with the sale window depending on platform:

PlayStation: November 16–30; Base game only

Epic Games Store: November 17–December 1; Base game, Deluxe Edition, Deluxe Edition Upgrade

Xbox: November 19–December 3; Base game, Deluxe Edition, Deluxe Edition Upgrade

Steam: November 19–December 3; Base game, Deluxe Edition, Deluxe Edition Upgrade

The game normally sells for $40 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Epic, Steam, and Nvidia GeForce NOW).

Flickering Flames Part 1 lands November 24

Update 2.7 arrives next week, on November 24, with Part 1 of the two-part Flickering Flames Raider project. The event warms Toledo in a celebration of light: with hopes of a festive gathering of all four contradas, Celeste is preparing a special dinner, and Raiders complete three steps to help her get ready. Each step pays out weapons and weapon mods, with additional cosmetic rewards coming in Part 2. The Nessuno Set — outfit, backpack, and backpack charm — is also headed to the in-game store rotation with the update.

The fixes that matter

2.6.0 is mostly a fixes patch, and several of the fixes target the kind of bug that ends a run unfairly:

• Invisible players: fixed two separate cases where a Raider could appear invisible to others — one tied to entering and quickly exiting the Gondola, one that could happen mid-round.

• Revive protection: enemies could knock a player out immediately after a defibrillator revive; being revived now properly prevents knockouts.

• Road Warrior skill: it can now recycle Weapon Amplification Modules and Candleberries during raids as intended.

• Vaulting stamina: vaulting no longer drains jump stamina, and the "Vaults on Vaults on Vaults" skill no longer drains any stamina.

• Hydra vs. lures: the Hydra now only aims some of its weapons at Lure Grenades, still targeting players with the rest.

• Snap Hook: the description now states the correct 18m range (previously listed as 20m).

• Stiletto: weight reduced from 7 to 6.

• Scoped aiming: aiming down sights with scoped weapons could shift aim sideways; aim now stays aligned with the crosshair entering and exiting ADS.

• Inventory: items can now be dropped by dragging them outside the inventory, and a gamepad looting bug that could delete a stack when interrupted is fixed.

• Outpost: the Outpost can now be correctly upgraded to Level 4, fixing a case where it could not be fully upgraded.

• Codex: a new "Times Revived By A Stranger" stat is on the player stats page.

Lighting and exposure also got a pass on Spaceport and Buried City, aimed at clearer visibility looking from interiors to exteriors and in dark interiors, and collision fixes landed across Pendola Pass, Spaceport, Riven Tides, and Stella Montis.

A year after launch, the cadence is the story as much as any single patch: 2.6.0 lands, 2.7 follows a week later, and the game keeps getting seasonal events and systemic fixes rather than coasting on its launch audience.

Darcy Kuemper's 40th career shutout — 29 saves and a penalty-shot stop — blanks the Bruins and ends the Kings' skid

By Matt

Darcy Kuemper stopped all 29 shots he faced, including Morgan Geekie's third-period penalty shot, for his 40th career shutout as the Kings beat Boston 3-0 at TD Garden, snapping a four-game losing streak.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Darcy Kuemper picked the right night to be perfect. The Los Angeles Kings goaltender stopped all 29 shots he faced — including a third-period penalty shot — for his 40th career shutout as Los Angeles beat the Boston Bruins 3-0 at TD Garden on Tuesday night, snapping a four-game losing streak.

It was his first shutout of the season, and it made him the fifth active goalie to reach 40. He got there faster than any of the other four: 501 games played, passing Connor Hellebuyck's 516.

"The guys were doing a great job in front of me, and I felt like I was able to see every shot," Kuemper said. "When we're boxing out like that it makes the goalie's job a lot easier."

The save

The shutout nearly ended at 9:51 of the third. Morgan Geekie was hooked by Drew Doughty on a breakaway and awarded a penalty shot with the Kings up 2-0. Geekie tried a forehand shot from in close. Kuemper made a glove save.

"I was just trying to be as big as I could," Kuemper said. "Obviously, he's a great shooter, so I wanted to take away as much of the net as I could and got a piece of it."

Penalty shots barely dent him: he has allowed only one goal in seven career penalty shots against.

The Bruins had a penalty shot of their own earlier — Quinton Byfield was tripped by Mason Lohrei on a breakaway at 5:56 of the second — but Michael DiPietro made a sprawling glove save on Byfield's forehand-backhand deke. DiPietro finished with 19 saves in the loss.

The goals

Mats Zuccarello opened the scoring at 15:46 of the first, beating a screened DiPietro short side from the left circle. It was the second consecutive game Zuccarello has scored — at 39, he joins Jarome Iginla, Luc Robitaille and Corey Perry as Kings who have scored in consecutive games at age 39 or older.

Andre Lee made it 2-0 at 16:35 of the second, redirecting a Scott Laughton centering pass in with his knee after Hampus Lindholm's clearing attempt was intercepted at the hash mark. Erik Gustafsson — back after missing three games with an undisclosed injury — scored into the empty net at 16:53 of the third for the final margin, with Kuemper picking up an assist on the play. Gustafsson also had a goal and an assist on the night.

The context

The Kings needed this one badly. They entered the night 6-11-2, losers of four straight, and got a road game exactly the way coach Peter Laviolette drew it up: desperate, blocking shots, backchecking, and a goalie who saw everything.

"We played a really good 40 minutes, and we didn't want to play the next 17 minutes like we did the first three minutes of the third period," Laviolette said. "I thought we responded well to both. I thought we did a really good job right in front of Darcy, and Darcy made some really big saves."

Boston, meanwhile, lost its third straight for the first time this season and fell to 13-7-1. Coach Marco Sturm was blunt: "We got more and more frustrated and made some mental mistakes and lost the game. I knew if we scored one, we would score two, but that goal never came."

What it means

Forty shutouts is a career milestone, but the timing is the story: a struggling team, a four-game skid, a road game in a building where the last eight meetings between these teams had all gone to overtime or a shootout. Kuemper ended that pattern with a clean sheet — and did it faster than any active goalie in the league.

TSL Bets parlay: Nikola Jokic OVER 24.5 points + Shai Gilgeous-Alexander OVER 30.5 points (~+300)

By Matt

Two props, two scoring stars. Nikola Jokic OVER 24.5 points (-105) at home against a Boston frontcourt with no answer for him, plus Shai Gilgeous-Alexander OVER 30.5 points (+104) at home against Atlanta — about +300 combined.

The game slips

Boston Celtics (11-3) at Denver Nuggets (7-5)

The bet

2-leg parlay (~+300): Nikola Jokic OVER 24.5 points (-105, Fanatics) + Shai Gilgeous-Alexander OVER 30.5 points (+104, best price Splash Sports via OPTIMAL)

Updated 7:40 PM ET: Cade Cunningham is questionable tonight with right knee soreness, so the Cade Cunningham OVER 24.5 leg is out and Nikola Jokic OVER 24.5 is in. The Gilgeous-Alexander leg is unchanged. The swap was made before either game tipped.

Why these legs

Both legs are props with real matchup edges. Jokic scored 28 on Monday, has cleared 35.5 points plus rebounds in five of his last six, and faces a Boston center rotation of Queta, Robinson and Garza — the softest frontcourt matchup on the board tonight. The line is 24.5 at -105. OPTIMAL projects Gilgeous-Alexander for 30.6 points at home against an Atlanta team giving up 116.1 a game, and he has gone over 30.5 in 5 of his last 10 while averaging 33.4 over his last seven.

Neither leg depends on the other — different games, different teams, different defenses. Both are plus-money or near it, so the parlay pays about +300 instead of the chalky +150 you get from stacking favorites. That is the juice rule working as intended: two real edges, one ticket.

The honest caveats

Jokic's season average (24.1) and his career mark against Boston (23.1) both sit below 24.5 — this is a matchup and form play, not a season-average edge, and one projection has him at 24.4, a hair under the line. Gilgeous-Alexander's models disagree with each other: one has him at 29 points tonight, below the line, even as his last-seven average says over. Boston is favored in Denver, so a Celtics run could cut Jokic's late minutes, and a blowout in Oklahoma City could do the same to Gilgeous-Alexander. A parlay needs both legs, and either one can sink it alone.

By Matt

The Lakers are 13-2 on a nine-game win streak, Austin Reaves is out, Utah's frontcourt is stripped by injuries, and Luka Doncic leads the league at 38.8 points per game. The play: Doncic OVER 37.5 points (+104) against the 2-13 Jazz.

The game slip

Utah Jazz (2-13) at Los Angeles Lakers (13-2)

Wednesday, 10:00 PM ET — Crypto.com Arena, Los Angeles

• Spread: Lakers -10.5

• Total: 229

• Moneyline: Lakers -455 / Jazz +360

• Odds source: Median across 12 US books via MoneyMaverick; moneyline via SportyTrader odds comparison, November 18

Injury report — Lakers: G Austin Reaves OUT (left heel bruise, per ESPN's morning injury report — the Lakers' second-leading scorer at 24.7 PPG). C Walker Kessler game-time decision (right lower-leg soreness; coach JJ Redick said he expects Kessler to be available).

Injury report — Jazz: F Lauri Markkanen OUT (two non-displaced right-hand fractures). F Jaren Jackson Jr. OUT (right MCL tear). C Jusuf Nurkic OUT (partial plantar plate tear, right foot). C Jaxson Hayes OUT (left knee strain). Utah's frontcourt is stripped to Tony Bradley and Kyle Filipowski behind Mo Bamba.

Storylines: The Lakers have won nine straight and own the best record in the NBA at 13-2, averaging 127.4 points a game at home, where they are 6-1. Doncic leads the league at 38.8 points per game and has scored at least 30 in 11 straight games — and he hung 52 on Utah in a 132-123 win at Salt Lake City on October 25. The Jazz are 2-13 and 1-6 on the road, conceding 117.3 points a game away from home, and they are on the second night of a back-to-back after snapping their 12-game losing streak behind Brice Sensabaugh's 40 on Tuesday. Both teams played last night; neither has a rest edge.

The bet

Luka Doncic OVER 37.5 points (+104, best price Novig via OPTIMAL)

Why this prop

Doncic is the NBA's scoring leader at 38.8 points per game, and the line sits below his average. He has gone over 37.5 points in 7 of his last 10 games, and OPTIMAL projects him for 37.4 against Utah — right at the number, with the best available price paying plus money.

The injury report is the engine here again. With Reaves out, the shot-creation load shifts almost entirely onto Doncic, and Kessler's status is uncertain. The matchup is the softest possible landing spot: Utah is 2-13 with its frontcourt gutted by injuries, and Doncic already scored 52 against this same team three weeks ago. He is taking 13.3 three-point attempts a game and making 5.4 of them.

This is the props-first single by the book: a player prop with a real matchup edge, a line sitting below the scoring leader's average, and plus-money juice on the over.

The honest caveats

A blowout could trim Doncic's fourth-quarter minutes — the Lakers are laying 10.5, and if this one gets away early, the fourth quarter belongs to the bench. He also played 41 and a half minutes in an overtime game last night, so the legs are a real question on the second night of a back-to-back. And the projection is not a slam dunk: it sits at 37.4 against a 37.5 line, and one model range has him lower. If Reaves ends up playing after all, some usage comes back. The edge is real, but it is an edge, not a lock.

The record

TSL Bets is 21-34 in November, 25-55 all-time. Props are 7-2 in November — the only winning singles category — that's why the daily single is a prop.

If you or someone you know has a gambling problem, call 1-800-GAMBLER.

Collectibles · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:02 AM ET

A serialized Golden Chocobo just sold for a reported $1.4 million — more than five times the card's previous record

By Matt

A PSA 10 Golden Chocobo, copy 47 of 77, reportedly changed hands in a $1.4 million private sale — shattering the card's previous confirmed record of $250,000. The buyer is not identified, and no settlement documents have been published, so the figure is an attributed private-sale price, not an auction result.

The sale

A serialized Golden Chocobo from Magic: The Gathering's Final Fantasy set reportedly sold for $1.4 million in a private sale — a new reported high for the card, and more than five times its previous confirmed record.

The sale was reported by Collectr, the card-tracking app, and covered by MTG Rocks on November 17. The card is copy 47 of 77, graded PSA Gem Mint 10, and it also carries an MBA Gold Diamond evaluation — a second independent grading that marks it among the best examples of its kind.

The seller was identified as Adam Cai, known as Pristine_Collectibles, who was tagged in Collectr's announcement. MTG content creator Ben Bateman posted on November 17 about meeting Cai at MagicCon: Atlanta and discussing the deal.

The caveat

This is a reported private sale, not a public auction. No buyer identity has been published, and no settlement document or payment record has been made public. The $1.4 million figure is attributed — real reporting, from a named seller and a named source, but with less public price discovery than a fully documented auction result.

That matters for what the number means. With only 77 serialized copies in existence, one sale cannot establish a reliable market price for the other 76. The previous confirmed Golden Chocobo sale was $250,000 — less than a quarter of this new figure. If the $1.4 million holds up, it resets the ceiling for the card overnight. If it does not, it is a rumor with a big number attached.

The card

The Golden Chocobo — the serialized gold-stamped version of Traveling Chocobo — is the premier chase card of the Final Fantasy set, Magic's best-selling release of all time. Only 77 copies were printed, each uniquely numbered, and they appear only in English-language Collector Boosters. The card carries no rules text at all, a first for a serialized Magic card, and no borders — just the golden bird, the number, and the art.

It is the set's answer to The One Ring: a single serialized chase card that became the face of the entire release, with every Collector Booster opened in part because it might be inside.

What it means

Whether or not $1.4 million becomes the card's settled price, the report itself is the story: a modern Magic card, printed in 2025, is now being talked about in the same breath as the game's most expensive pieces ever. The serialized-chase era that started with The One Ring has a new headline number — and every other Golden Chocobo owner just watched their card's ceiling move.

iShowSpeed just won Streamer of the Year at the Esports Awards — his second Streamer of the Year trophy in five days

By Matt

iShowSpeed won Streamer of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026 in Miami on Monday night, beating Kai Cenat, CaseOh, Jynxzi and Caedrel — five days after taking the same title at the Streamer Awards in Los Angeles.

The night

Darren "iShowSpeed" Watkins Jr. won Streamer of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026 on Monday night, November 17, at the Adrienne Arsht Center in Miami.

He beat 11 other nominees for the title: Kai Cenat, CaseOh, Jynxzi, Caedrel, OhnePixel, JasonTheWeen, Cinna, StableRonaldo, Snax Gaming, Coringa and TheBurntPeanut.

It is his second Streamer of the Year trophy in five days. Last Thursday, November 13, Speed won the same title at the sixth annual Streamer Awards in Los Angeles — his third straight win there — taking three trophies on the night. The Esports Awards is a separate ceremony, esports' own biggest night, and Speed just swept the top streamer prize at both of them in the same week.

The other winners

Marc "Caedrel" Lamont was honored as Esports Personality of the Year, and Jynxzi took Esports Content Creator of the Year. The ceremony returned to Miami for what the organizers call the biggest and most prestigious night in esports, with the night's winners announced across the full list of categories.

The year

The award caps a year in which Speed kept expanding past streaming. He did his World Cup Tour this year, partnering with FIFA to livestream soccer fans around the globe, and last month he became an executive producer on "The Eyes of Ghana," a documentary alongside former President Barack Obama and Michelle Obama.

He also has GTA 6 on the calendar: Speed and Kai Cenat have both announced plans to stream the game when it releases — Cenat starting at 8 p.m. ET on November 18, Speed an hour later at 9 p.m. ET.

What it means

Two ceremonies, two Streamer of the Year trophies, five days apart. Whatever you think of the awards circuit, the industry just told the same story twice in one week: right now, the biggest streamer in the world is Speed — and the gap between him and everyone else is not particularly close.

Gaming · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:02 AM ET

GTA 6 leads The Game Awards 2026 with eight nominations — including Game of the Year — two days before it even launches

By Matt

Grand Theft Auto VI picked up eight nominations at The Game Awards 2026, the most of any game, with Game of the Year among them — revealed on Tuesday, two days before the game launches on November 19. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem follow with six each.

The nominees are out

The Game Awards revealed its full 2026 nominee list on Tuesday, November 17, in a livestream hosted by creator Geoff Keighley — and the game at the top of the list is not out yet.

Grand Theft Auto VI leads the field with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Performance for Manni L. Perez as Lucia, and Best Action/Adventure Game. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem follow with six nominations each, and Phantom Blade Zero has five.

The Game of the Year field is six games deep this year instead of the usual five, after a tie in the voting: 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto VI, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

The timing

GTA 6 launches on Thursday, November 19 — two days after the nominations were announced, and one day before The Game Awards' eligibility cutoff of 9 p.m. PT on Friday, November 20. That is the whole reason it qualifies at all: the game had to be commercially available by the cutoff, and it clears the line with a single day to spare.

It is a strange position for a frontrunner. Nobody outside Rockstar's review program has played the game yet, and the winners will not be announced until the ceremony on December 10 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles — three weeks after launch, when millions of players will have had their say in the other direction. Fan voting is open now and closes December 9 at 6 p.m. PT, with the winners decided by a global jury of more than 160 media publications and creator outlets combined with the fan vote.

The context

This is not GTA 6's first time at the show. It won Most Anticipated Game in both 2024 and 2025, back when the wait was the story. Now the wait is over and the game is the story — and it is competing in the categories that actually judge a game, not just the hype around one.

The other contenders are not pushovers. Control Resonant is up for Game of the Year, Best Game Direction and Best Narrative. Resident Evil Requiem matches it at six nominations. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Nintendo's remake, which sold 5.2 million copies in four days — rounds out a Game of the Year field with no obvious weak link.

Watch the trailer

Watch on YouTube

Source: Grand Theft Auto VI Launch Trailer — Rockstar Games on YouTube. The official launch trailer: Jason and Lucia, one week out from November 19.

What it means

Eight nominations for a game nobody has played is either a coronation or a dare. By December 10, the jury will have had three weeks with the actual game — and so will everyone else. If GTA 6 is as good as the nominations assume, the ceremony is a formality. If it is not, this list will look very different in hindsight.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:01 AM ET

Connor McDavid's point streak is at 23 — tied with Wayne Gretzky for the fourth-longest season-opening run in NHL history

By Matt

Connor McDavid scored a power-play goal in Edmonton's 5-2 win at Florida to extend his season-opening point streak to 23 games, tying Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 run for the fourth-longest in NHL history — and passing Dany Heatley's 22.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Connor McDavid does not need long to make history. Three minutes and 33 seconds into the Edmonton Oilers' game against the Florida Panthers on Tuesday night, he scored a power-play goal — his 13th of the season — and extended his season-opening point streak to 23 games.

The Oilers won 5-2 at Amerant Bank Arena, their sixth straight victory. McDavid finished with a goal and an assist, giving him 55 points on the season — 13 goals and 42 assists — still the league lead by a wide margin.

The list

Twenty-three games ties Wayne Gretzky's 1988-89 run for the fourth-longest season-opening point streak in NHL history. The full list ahead of him now reads like a shrine:

• Wayne Gretzky, 51 games (1983-84)

• Wayne Gretzky, 30 games (1982-83)

• Mats Sundin, 30 games (1992-93)

• Wayne Gretzky, 23 games (1988-89)

• Connor McDavid, 23 games (2026-27)

One game ago, McDavid was tied with Dany Heatley (22 games, 2005-06) for fifth. Tuesday's goal moved him past Heatley and level with Gretzky — the fourth name on the list who is not Gretzky or Sundin, and the only active player anywhere near it.

The goal also moved McDavid past Gretzky for the most power-play points in Oilers franchise history.

The season

This is the best start of McDavid's career, and the numbers keep stacking up behind the streak. He was the first player to reach 50 points in 21 games or fewer since Mario Lemieux did it in 18 games in 1995-96. He tied Gretzky as the fastest player ever to 40 assists in a season, doing it in 22 games. He is on pace for a season that would challenge Gretzky's single-season scoring record of 215 points, set in 1985-86.

Kasperi Kapanen opened the scoring for Edmonton on Tuesday and finished with a goal and two assists. The Oilers are 16-3-3.

What it means

The next milestone is seven games away: 30 would tie Gretzky's 1982-83 run and Sundin's 1992-93 mark. The 51-game record is not a realistic target for anyone — Gretzky's 1983-84 run is the most untouchable number in the sport. But McDavid is now sitting at a table with exactly two other names on it, and he gets his next chance on Thursday against the Tampa Bay Lightning, where a point would move him into sole possession of fourth place all by himself.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:01 AM ET

Matthew Schaefer, 19, just became the third teenage defenseman in NHL history with a hat trick — and the first Islander to do it since Denis Potvin in 1982

By Matt

Matthew Schaefer scored his first career hat trick — at 19 years and 73 days old, the second-youngest defenseman ever to do it — as the Islanders beat the Blue Jackets 5-1 at UBS Arena for their third straight win.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The hats rained down at UBS Arena, and they were raining for a teenager who plays defense.

Matthew Schaefer scored his first career hat trick on Tuesday night, leading the New York Islanders to a 5-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. At 19 years and 73 days old, he became the second-youngest defenseman in NHL history to record a hat trick — behind only Phil Housley, who was 18 years and 320 days old when he did it — and just the third teenage defenseman ever to do it, after Housley in January 1983 and Hannu Virta in March 1983.

He is also the first Islanders defenseman with a hat trick since Denis Potvin on March 4, 1982, and only the third in franchise history, joining Denis and his brother Jean Potvin.

Schaefer opened his scoring 1:34 into the second period, ripping a shot from the slot past Cam Talbot. He added a second at 7:01 of the third, backhanding home a rebound off Ryan Pulock's shot after Zach Werenski had cut the lead to 2-1. Then he completed it with an empty-netter at 16:08 of the third, slamming into the boards in elation as the hats flew.

He finished with three goals and nine shots in 23:23 of ice time.

The season

The hat trick is not a bolt from the blue — it is the loudest night yet of a breakout. All nine of Schaefer's goals this season have come in the past 11 games, and he has at least one point in six straight. Through 20 games he has 24 points while averaging 26:58 of ice time a night.

The career numbers are already historic. He now has 32 goals before turning 20, the second-most ever by a teenage defenseman behind Housley's 46. The reigning Calder Trophy winner and No. 1 overall pick of the 2025 draft is playing like a franchise defenseman who happens to still be a teenager.

The game around him

Anthony Duclair opened the scoring with a power-play goal in the final minute of the first period and finished with a goal and an assist. Tony DeAngelo added a goal and an assist of his own, Mathew Barzal had two assists, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 28 shots. Werenski scored the only Columbus goal, and Talbot made 36 saves in the loss.

The win was the Islanders' third straight and moved them to 10-6-4, with points in five straight games.

What it means

A defenseman scoring three goals in a game is rare. A 19-year-old defenseman doing it puts him in a group of three in the entire history of the league — and the other two did it more than 40 years ago. The Islanders have not had a defenseman do this since Potvin, and Potvin is the standard every Islanders defenseman gets measured against. Schaefer is 19, and he is already in that conversation.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:01 AM ET

Mikko Rantanen factored into all four Stars goals — the tying goal with five seconds left, then the OT-winner assist — in a 4-3 stunner over Vegas

By Matt

Mikko Rantanen had a goal and three assists — a point on every Dallas goal — including the tying goal with five seconds left in regulation and the assist on Miro Heiskanen's overtime winner, as the Stars erased a 3-1 deficit in the final 1:18 to beat the Golden Knights 4-3.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Dallas Stars were dead. Down 3-1 to the Vegas Golden Knights with less than two minutes to play in regulation at T-Mobile Arena on Tuesday night, goalie pulled, season's road trip hanging in the balance. Then Mikko Rantanen took the game over.

Rantanen finished with a goal and three assists — a point on all four Dallas goals — as the Stars scored twice in the final 1:18 of regulation and won it 4-3 in overtime.

Wyatt Johnston started the comeback at 18:42 of the third, scoring 6-on-5 from Roope Hintz and Rantanen to make it 3-2. Then, with five seconds left, Rantanen threw a shot toward the net from along the right boards. It deflected in off Vegas defenseman Rasmus Andersson. Tie game, 3-3.

In overtime, Rantanen did it again — feeding Miro Heiskanen for the winner at 3:36, a tap-in from the bottom of the left circle into an open net after a scramble near the crease.

The return

Heiskanen's goal was a story on its own. The defenseman was playing his first game back after missing five with an upper-body injury, and the overtime winner was the fourth of his career. He logged 26:44 over 25 shifts, blocked three shots, and scored on his only shot of the night.

Vegas had controlled the game until the collapse. William Karlsson scored twice — his first two-goal game since October 16, 2025 — and Brett Howden added a goal as the Golden Knights built a 3-1 third-period lead. Nils Lundkvist had pulled Dallas within one at 10:59 of the third, finishing a rush off a Rantanen feed, but Howden answered 32 seconds later to restore the two-goal cushion.

Then the final 1:18 happened. Two 6-on-5 goals, 73 seconds apart, both with Jake Oettinger on the bench for the extra attacker. Oettinger finished with 24 saves.

The context

The win was Dallas' third straight and moved the Stars to 13-6-2 — and within two points of Vegas in the Western standings. It was also their fifth overtime win in 21 games. Rantanen's line — one goal, three assists, plus-4, five shots in 24:24 — is the kind of night that defines a player's value to a team: he did not just produce, he touched every goal that mattered.

Vegas, meanwhile, lost its third straight (0-1-2) and fell to 13-6-4. The two teams do it all over again Thursday night in the same building.

What it means

A two-goal lead with 1:18 left is supposed to be over. Rantanen made it a footnote. When one player factors into every goal in a comeback win — the setup, the equalizer, and the overtime winner — that is not a hot streak, that is a takeover.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:00 AM ET

Quentin Grimes drops a career-high 47 — 10 threes, a game-tying bomb with 1.7 left — as the Lakers rally from 18 down to beat the Hornets in OT

By Matt

Quentin Grimes scored a career-high 47 points, including 21 in the fourth quarter and the game-tying three with 1.7 seconds left, as the short-handed Lakers came back from 18 down to beat Charlotte 118-114 in overtime for their ninth straight win.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Quentin Grimes had never scored 40 points in an NBA game. Then the Lakers needed him to save one.

Grimes scored a career-high 47 points — 16-of-24 from the field, 10-of-14 from three — and buried the game-tying three with 1.7 seconds left in regulation as Los Angeles came back from 18 down to beat the Charlotte Hornets 118-114 in overtime at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday night. It was the Lakers' ninth consecutive win, and they are 13-2 with the best record in the NBA.

The shot itself was disbelief made real. Luka Doncic brought the ball up with under 10 seconds left, the Lakers trailing 111-108, and found Grimes wide open on the right wing. Grimes had already outscored the Hornets 18-17 by himself in the quarter.

"I don't know why they left me open," Grimes said after the game. "I was like, 'Oh yeah, that's cash. I was too open.'"

The 10 threes are a career high, and they put Grimes next to Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers ever to hit 10 or more in a single game. Bryant hit 12 against Seattle in 2003.

The fourth quarter

The Lakers were lifeless for three quarters. They trailed 94-81 entering the fourth, down 18 in the last minute of the third, and were missing their second- and third-leading scorers — Austin Reaves (left heel bruise) and Walker Kessler (right leg soreness) both sat out.

Then Doncic went to the bench for the first six minutes of the final frame, and Grimes took the game over. He scored 21 points in the quarter, including 15 to Charlotte's five over a six-and-a-half-minute stretch that erased a 14-point deficit. When Doncic returned, he kept calling off JJ Redick's plays just to get Grimes the ball.

"Luka, when he got back in the game in the fourth, he kept calling off every play I was calling and just saying, 'No, I'm trying to get Q the ball!'" Redick said. "He recognized what was happening. The hot-hand theory — it's a real thing. It definitely was a real thing tonight."

Doncic finished with 36 points of his own on 13-of-34 shooting, his 11th consecutive game with at least 30. The two combined for 83 points and 15 threes, and the Lakers outscored Charlotte 37-20 across the fourth quarter and overtime, holding the Hornets to three points in the extra session.

Grimes iced it himself in overtime, disrupting an inbounds pass meant for Royce O'Neale with 17.4 seconds left, then making both free throws. Matisse Thybulle added three steals, the last with 8.8 seconds to go.

The context

The win made the Lakers just the fourth team in league history with three different players scoring 40-plus through the first 15 games of a season — Grimes joining Doncic and Reaves. It also kept them unbeaten in November despite playing without two starters, on a night when the supporting cast had to carry real weight: Kevon Looney, Jarred Vanderbilt and two-way player Carson Cooper, playing his first game as a Laker, combined for 19 rebounds with Kessler out.

There was a personal layer to the night, too. Grimes' mother, Tonja Stelly, was in the stands the day after her 60th birthday. He gave her his game-worn uniform afterward and admitted he had tried to get 60 points for her 60th. He came 13 short — and nobody in the building was complaining.

He also did it a week after dislocating the pinkie finger on his shooting hand, an injury that cost him two straight games. Collin Sexton, who scored 10 off the bench, said the locker room has spent weeks telling Grimes to let it fly. Tuesday night, he finally did.

Charlotte, for its part, did almost everything right for three quarters. Brandon Miller scored 28, Naz Reid added 23 points and 11 rebounds, and the Hornets led in every period before the fourth. It is their ninth loss in 10 games.

What it means

Nine straight wins, the league's best record, and now a night where the third option became the hero. The Lakers keep finding a different guy to win the game — and Tuesday it was the one who had never scored 40 before, against a team that left him open with the game on the line.

Up next: the Lakers host the Utah Jazz on Wednesday night at Crypto.com Arena, the second night of a back-to-back.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 8:00 AM ET

The Pistons just ended the Spurs' 12-game win streak — Cade's 27, Jenkins' 25, and a fourth quarter San Antonio never solved

By Matt

Cade Cunningham scored 27 points, Daniss Jenkins added 25 off the bench, and Ausar Thompson finished a rebound shy of a triple-double as Detroit rallied from 14 down to beat San Antonio 105-93, ending the Spurs' 12-game winning streak.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The San Antonio Spurs had not lost since October 23. They had won 12 straight, owned the best record in the West, and had Victor Wembanyama rolling toward another MVP case. The Detroit Pistons walked into Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night, fell behind by 14, and beat them anyway, 105-93.

Cade Cunningham led Detroit with 27 points, five rebounds and six assists. Daniss Jenkins added 25 points, five rebounds and five assists off the bench. Ausar Thompson finished a rebound shy of a triple-double with 14 points, 12 assists and five steals.

The Pistons trailed 55-54 at halftime and were down six entering the fourth, 78-72. Then they held San Antonio to 21 fourth-quarter points, led by as many as 11 multiple times in the period, and never let the Spurs' final push get closer than five. Dylan Harper cut it to five with a layup at the 2:35 mark, then slipped and fell heading downcourt with a little more than a minute left, suffering an apparent groin injury. Detroit pulled away from there.

"Have fun. Play basketball. It's another game," Cunningham said after the game. "Obviously, they're a good team, but nobody in that locker room has fear in his heart for anybody. So it's just about coming out here, playing basketball, doing what we do best, executing our game plan."

The streak

Twelve straight wins is the kind of run that starts showing up in franchise history books. Per the Spurs, it was their 25th double-digit win streak since the 1976-77 season, their first in the NBA after moving from the ABA — the most such streaks in the league, ahead of the Lakers (21), Celtics (16), Cavaliers (15) and Thunder (14). The NBA record is 33, set by the 1971-72 Lakers.

The loss drops San Antonio to 12-3, still among the strongest early-season teams in the West. It also held the Spurs below 100 points for the first time this season — 93 was their lowest scoring total of the year.

Wembanyama had 25 points and 18 rebounds in the loss, his 11th double-double of the season. He was blunt afterward: "We didn't do the right things. I think we should have been smarter. As soon as we stepped off the court after the end of the fourth quarter, things looked pretty straightforward and our mistakes looked kinda obvious."

The context

This was not a fluke night for Detroit. The Pistons shot 49 percent from the field, handed out 31 assists, and improved to 9-4 — third in the East — with a 6-2 road record. They have won three of four, and they did this one on the second night of a back-to-back, a night after Cade's 52-point game against Washington last week made him the first player in NBA history with 50 points and 10 assists and zero turnovers in a game.

Jenkins' 25 was the second-half engine: Detroit's bench outplayed San Antonio's depth all night, and the Pistons' defense held a team averaging well over 110 to its worst offensive night of the season.

What it means

Streaks end. The question was always who would be the team to do it, and Detroit answered it with defense, depth and a star who wanted the moment. The Spurs are still 12-3 and still terrifying. But the "when will they lose?" watch is over — and the team that ended it is 9-4 and playing like it belongs in the East's top tier.

Up next: the Pistons visit the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night. The Spurs host the Clippers on Thursday.

Sports · Nov 18, 2026 · 3:07 AM ET

Sensabaugh drops 40 to snap Utah's skid

By Matt

Brice Sensabaugh came off the bench and scored 40 points — 25 in the fourth quarter — as the Utah Jazz beat the LA Clippers 132-107 on Tuesday night, snapping a 12-game losing streak and becoming the youngest player in NBA history with 40 points, 10 rebounds and eight threes in a game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Utah Jazz had not won a game in nearly a month. Then Brice Sensabaugh came off the bench and took over the fourth quarter.

Sensabaugh scored a season-high 40 points — 25 of them in the final period — as Utah beat the Los Angeles Clippers 132-107 at Intuit Dome on Tuesday night. The win snapped a 12-game losing streak and gave the Jazz just their second victory of the season, improving them to 2-13. It was also their first road win of the season after an 0-6 start away from home, and their first win of any kind since a 120-119 decision over New Orleans on October 23.

The game was tight for three quarters. Utah led just 88-86 heading into the fourth, then blew it open. The Jazz outscored the Clippers 44-21 in the final 12 minutes, shooting 18-for-22 from the floor in the period. Sensabaugh sparked a game-changing 20-2 surge — including a 16-0 run midway through the quarter — with a pull-up jumper when Utah led 93-91, scoring 13 points in that stretch alone.

He finished 16-for-21 from the field and 8-for-11 from three, the eight makes a career high, adding 11 rebounds, five assists and a block. Keyonte George added 30 points and 11 assists, and Utah finished with a season-high 20 three-pointers on 38 attempts, shooting 58.3 percent from the floor as a team. Brook Lopez led the Clippers with 23 points and six rebounds in the loss, dropping Los Angeles to 4-9.

The history

The line put Sensabaugh in the record book. At 23 years and 18 days old, he became the youngest player in NBA history to total 40 or more points, 10 or more rebounds and eight or more three-pointers in a single game.

The 40 was three points shy of his career high — and his third career 40-point game — but this was his first 40-point double-double, and the first time he had done it coming off the bench. For a Jazz team that has been injury-plagued and short on bright spots during a 2-13 start, a 23-year-old reserve rewriting a record that young is the kind of night worth remembering long after the losing streak is forgotten.

What's next

Utah visits the Lakers on Wednesday, with three more games on the schedule this week. The skid is over. The question now is whether the youngest 40-10-8 night in league history was a one-off explosion or the start of something bigger for Sensabaugh.

Sports · Nov 17, 2026 · 11:41 PM ET

Cutter Gauthier's hat trick makes it 10 straight games with a goal — one shy of Selanne's Ducks record — as the Blues win a wild 8-6 one

By Matt

Cutter Gauthier scored three times in St. Louis — the last one with the goalie pulled and 41 seconds left — to stretch his goal streak to 10 straight games, one shy of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record, in an 8-6 loss to the Blues.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Cutter Gauthier did everything except win the game. The Anaheim Ducks winger scored three times at Enterprise Center on Tuesday night — a slap shot early in the second, a power-play snap shot late in the second, and a wrist shot with the goalie pulled and 41 seconds left — for his fourth hat trick of the season and a goal in his 10th consecutive game, the longest goal streak in the NHL in 29 years. The St. Louis Blues still won, 8-6.

The hat trick goal was the loudest of the night even in a loss. Down 7-4, the Ducks got a power-play goal from Mikael Granlund with 1:25 left — a 6-on-4 with the goalie already pulled — and Gauthier — fed by Troy Terry and Jackson LaCombe — beat Jordan Binnington from the right wing to make it 7-6 with 41 seconds on the clock. The building had three seconds to believe in a comeback before Pavel Buchnevich scored into the empty net to seal it.

Gauthier finished with three goals and an assist on eight shots in 23:54 of ice time. It was his fourth hat trick in 10 games, a run that already included three of them in eight days to start November. Four hat tricks in one calendar month is an NHL record — no player had ever done it before.

The streak

Ten straight games with a goal makes Gauthier the 21st player in NHL history to do it — and the first in 29 years. He entered the night with 16 goals in nine games, and he has 19 across the 10, with five assists for 24 points in the stretch. His point streak is now 12 games.

One more gets him a share of the franchise record. Teemu Selanne scored in 11 straight for Anaheim from October 21 to November 10, 1997, with 17 goals in that span. Gauthier can tie it Thursday night in Colorado, and break it Saturday in Utah.

The company keeps getting more ridiculous. Gauthier already joined Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux as the only players in 100 years with 14 or more goals in the first eight games of a calendar month, and he was the first player in NHL history with three hat tricks inside the first 10 days of a month — eight days, beating Phil Esposito's 13-day mark from December 1970. He entered Tuesday tied with Auston Matthews for the most goals through 20 games of a season by an active American player, at 18. He left St. Louis with 21 goals in 21 games.

November is turning into its own record chase. His 17 goals this month leave him three shy of the NHL record for a calendar month — 20, shared by Selanne (March 1993) and Joe Malone (February 1921) — with six November games left.

The game around him

It took eight different Blues to outscore him. St. Louis got goals from Jonatan Berggren, Connor McMichael, Robert Thomas, Dalibor Dvorsky, Jake Neighbours, Philip Broberg, Logan Mailloux and Buchnevich, with Thomas adding two assists for a three-point night. Mailloux's goal was the first of his NHL career. The Blues led 4-3 after two and 7-3 before Anaheim's late push made the final look closer than most of the night felt.

The Ducks got goals from Alex Killorn, Ian Moore — the first of his NHL career, unassisted — and Granlund alongside Gauthier's three, and they outshot St. Louis 31-28. But Ville Husso allowed seven goals on 24 shots, and even with Lukas Dostal stopping all three he faced in relief, the hole was too deep. Binnington made 25 saves for St. Louis.

Anaheim falls to 11-10. St. Louis improves to 10-9.

What it means

A hat trick in a loss is usually a footnote. This one isn't, because the streak is now the story of the NHL season — a 22-year-old winger scoring at a pace that has him standing next to Gretzky, Lemieux and Selanne in the record book, and doing it while his team keeps losing the games he takes over. The goals haven't been enough.

The record is right there, though. One goal in Denver on Thursday ties Selanne. One more in Utah on Saturday passes him. At this rate, betting against either feels foolish.

Up next: the Ducks visit the Avalanche on Thursday, November 19 at 9:00 PM ET, then the Mammoth in Utah on Saturday.

Deep Space 9 is Star Trek's breakout card

By Matt

Five Magic: The Gathering Star Trek cards have spiked since prerelease — and Deep Space 9 leads the way, climbing from $14.50 to $40 after Worlds put the new set through its paces.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The spike

Five cards from Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek have spiked in price in the few days since prerelease — and the headliner is the station itself. Deep Space 9 went from $14.50 at prerelease to $40, a jump of roughly 176% in under two weeks. A nine-mana mythic was always going to cost real money — but $40 caught everyone off guard.

The timing tells the story. Worlds, the biggest tournament of the year, kicked off on the set's release day, immediately putting the new cards to the test in high-level competitive play. The ones that performed spiked; the ones that didn't fell back. Five passed the test.

The five risers

Deep Space 9: $14.50; $40

Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy: $7.70; $23.50

Captain James T. Kirk: $6.50; $22

Anthropological Mission: $0.50; $8

The Naked Time: $0.50; $2.90

The foil market agrees with the direction: NerdSnack's TCG Market Movers board has the foil printing at $43.83, up from $18.60 over the November 10–17 window — a 136% move.

Why the station is worth it

Deep Space 9 is a nine-drop that pays you back the moment it lands. When it enters — and at the beginning of your upkeep — it exiles the top four cards of your library and puts every permanent exiled that way onto the battlefield. Up to four free permanents a turn is the kind of effect that ends games, and it's one you can cheat into play rather than hard-casting for nine.

It shines in the new spacecraft decks built around Captain Picard, sure — but the price is being driven by something wider: unlike most cards of its type, it doesn't need your deck to be all about rockets and charge counters. It fits Eldrazi shells and artifact decks, or really anything that can get to nine mana and wants a game-ender. A finisher that slots into existing shells instead of demanding a new one is exactly the kind of card that holds a price.

The Worlds effect

The other four risers all have the same fingerprint: they showed up at Worlds and did real work.

Anthropological Mission is the real shocker out of Atlanta. Stefan Schütz rode it to the Worlds title with an Izzet list running a full playset of a fifty-cent uncommon nobody had on their radar. Once it has three counters, it stops looting and starts netting a card every time you play a non-creature spell. Schütz's list leaned all the way into that: thirty instants and sorceries, zero creatures, and a deck that just buries opponents in cards once the Mission is online. A fifty-cent uncommon that won the biggest tournament of the year doesn't stay fifty cents.

The Naked Time caught the wave of Boros Pixie, the most-played deck of the weekend. It pumps a creature, gives it haste, and ramps you in red — strong enough that some players were openly asking if it should be banned. It isn't, and it's not even the set's best uncommon — but a card that strong in the format's most-played deck was never going to stay at prerelease pricing.

Captain James T. Kirk is the other half of that Boros story: an efficient, aggressive creature that generates a lot of value when your back is against the wall, and a key part of the deck that dominated Worlds weekend.

Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy is a useful ramp creature — and a beater in her own right in a long game — that has proven popular in a rising Selesnya Landfall deck, an archetype that appeared en masse at the recent tournament.

What it means

Prerelease pricing is a guess; Worlds is the answer key. The Star Trek set's early market was soft — most cards came down once packs started opening — but the five that proved themselves in competitive play went the other way, and the station went furthest of all. If the Worlds decks stay relevant, these prices have room; if the meta moves on, the uncommons that rode one tournament are the first to give it back.

Sports · Nov 17, 2026 · 8:04 AM ET

The winless Chargers bully the Ravens at the line, 23-20 — first win of the season, and no winless teams remain

By Matt

Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton ran for first-half touchdowns and the Los Angeles Chargers manhandled Baltimore at the line of scrimmage, outrushing the Ravens 160-16 in a 23-20 Monday night win — their first of the season, ending an 11-game losing streak dating to last season.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The combined 15 straight losses the Chargers and Ravens carried into Monday night was a record for a Monday night game. Somebody had to win. It was the team that hadn't won all season.

Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton ran for first-half touchdowns, and the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season by manhandling Baltimore at the line of scrimmage in a 23-20 victory at M&T Bank Stadium. The Chargers outrushed the Ravens 160-16 — and held Baltimore to zero rushing yards in the first half.

Herbert completed only 12 passes for 129 yards, but his 22-yard scoring run on the first Los Angeles possession gave the Chargers a lead they would not relinquish. He added 51 rushing yards on seven carries, and a week after taking a career-high eight sacks against Houston, he was brought down just twice.

Hampton's night

Hampton carried 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown — the first Charger to top 100 rushing yards this season, and the second 100-yard game of his young career. His touchdown came on fourth down from the 1 with 1:56 left in the half: initially stopped by linebacker Roquan Smith, he powered into the end zone with help from a couple of teammates to make it 17-7.

The drive was set up by a Del'Shawn Phillips interception in the second quarter. Fullback Scott Matlock opened lanes all night, and Hampton was the featured back in every sense — Hassan Haskins and Kimani Vidal combined for just five carries behind him.

The other side

Derrick Henry was held to 10 yards on 10 carries, although he did score two touchdowns — a 2-yarder that cut the lead to 10-7, and a 1-yarder that made it 23-20 with 10:23 left. The 10 yards were the second-fewest of his career in a game with 10 or more carries; the only worse night was 9 yards on 16 attempts against Houston on December 17, 2023.

Jacoby Brissett threw for 340 yards in his Baltimore debut, completing 33 of 49 passes with one interception — the second-highest passing total of his career. With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both on injured reserve, the Ravens traded for Brissett on November 6 in the hope the veteran could keep the offense functional. He did, mostly. The run game did not.

Baltimore began the game by going three-and-out three straight times, and the boos rained down on a team that has now lost seven of its last eight home games. The Ravens are 4-6 after a fifth straight loss, having started the season 4-1.

The finish

With the Chargers up 23-20, Baltimore's Zay Flowers — plagued by fumbling problems in his career — lost another one after catching a pass near the Los Angeles 45 with 2:03 remaining. Tarheeb Still stripped him, Elijah Molden recovered at the visitors' 46, and it was Flowers' first lost fumble of the season.

Herbert then threw to ex-Raven Charlie Kolar for the first down that all but ended the game. Baltimore got the ball back at its own 20 with 11 seconds left, Brissett completed a pass downfield, and his Hail Mary fell incomplete.

Cameron Dicker went 3-for-3 on field goals, including a 34-yarder that extended the lead to 20-10, and Dalvin Tomlinson added two sacks for a Chargers defense that set the tone from the first snap.

What it means

The Chargers are 1-8, and one win over a reeling Ravens team doesn't change what this season is. But an 11-game losing streak dating to last season — including a playoff loss — is over, and it ended with the kind of performance that travels: a line that dominated, a running back who carried the load, and a defense that made the play of the night when the game was on the line.

For Baltimore, the embarrassment is the story. A team that was supposed to be competing for Super Bowls is now 4-6, has lost five straight, and just got outrushed by 144 yards at home by a team that hadn't won a game. The Ravens visit Carolina on Sunday; the Chargers host the New York Jets.

Sports · Nov 17, 2026 · 8:04 AM ET

Jeremiah Fears, 20, becomes the youngest Pelican ever with a triple-double — New Orleans snaps its skid, 115-94 over Golden State

By Matt

Jeremiah Fears had 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists for his first career triple-double, and at 20 years and 33 days old he is the youngest player in Pelicans history to do it — passing Chris Paul's mark from April 2006 — as New Orleans snapped a six-game losing streak with a 115-94 win over Golden State.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Smoothie King Center crowd knew what was happening before the box score did. Late in the third quarter, Jeremiah Fears grabbed his 10th rebound, the building erupted, and a 20-year-old rookie had the first triple-double of his career — 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 115-94 win over the Golden State Warriors that snapped New Orleans' six-game losing streak.

Fears did it at 20 years and 33 days old. That makes him the youngest player in Pelicans franchise history to record a triple-double, passing a mark Chris Paul set at 20 years and 331 days on April 2, 2006 — a record that had stood for more than two decades. He is also the ninth-youngest player in NBA history to post one.

The game itself was never close. New Orleans led 35-11 after one quarter and pushed the lead as large as 31 in the third. Fears shot 6-of-13 from the field and 1-of-4 from three in 29 minutes, and by the time he sealed the milestone the only question left was the final margin.

The help around him

Saddiq Bey led the Pelicans with 23 points, hitting five threes, and Zion Williamson added 16. Yves Missi grabbed 14 rebounds in his second game back from a knee injury that sidelined him 11 games, and Derik Queen — drafted six spots after Fears — came off the bench for 17 points and 10 rebounds, tying a career high with four threes. Jeron Pierre Jr. added 10 points.

New Orleans shot 42.3 percent from the field and 15-of-40 from three, outscored Golden State 44-32 in the paint, and outrebounded the Warriors 57-50. It was the kind of complete night the Pelicans, now 5-10, have been waiting for all season.

The other side

Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored a game-high 28 points for Golden State, with Brandin Podziemski adding 15 and Gui Santos 12. But the Warriors shot 33.3 percent from the field and 11-of-46 from three, and this was their third straight loss — the second in a row by 20 or more, coming on the heels of a 123-85 defeat at San Antonio on Friday night.

Golden State is playing without Stephen Curry, sidelined at least two weeks with a right oblique tear suffered in a 115-108 loss at Houston on Wednesday. The gap between the Warriors with Curry and without him has been stark, and Monday night was the latest evidence.

What it means

A triple-double at 20 years and 33 days puts Fears in rare company — and passing Chris Paul to do it, in a Pelicans uniform, is the kind of line that follows a player. Paul's mark had survived every Pelican since, including Anthony Davis and Zion Williamson. Fears cleared it by nearly ten months.

The win matters too. Six straight losses had the Pelicans buried at the bottom of the West, and a 21-point win over a shorthanded Warriors team doesn't fix the season — but a franchise-record night from the seventh overall pick is exactly the kind of thing a rebuild is supposed to produce.

Up next: the Warriors visit Dallas on Wednesday, and the Pelicans host Detroit the same night.
