Warriors make history: first team ever to start 0-3 and win eight straight

By Matt

The Warriors crushed the Pelicans 138-87 for their eighth straight win — making them the first team in NBA history to start 0-3 and then win eight in a row.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Golden State Warriors beat the New Orleans Pelicans 138-87 at Chase Center on Monday night, and the 51-point margin was only the second-most interesting number on the board. The Warriors are now 8-3, winners of eight straight, after starting the season 0-3. No team in NBA history has ever done that before.

The last team to win seven straight after an 0-3 start was the 1950-51 Boston Celtics, in Red Auerbach's first season as coach. Golden State blew past them on Monday and kept going. It was a 6-0 homestand, capped by the fourth-largest margin of victory in franchise history and the biggest since a 157-101 win at Portland in April 2023.

Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 21 minutes with four threes. Brandin Podziemski added 25 with five threes and four assists. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg went for 23 points, 7 rebounds and 4 assists. Derik Queen led New Orleans with 16. Jordan Poole, back in the building where he won a ring, scored 7 points on 1-of-5 shooting in 33 minutes.

The context

The Pelicans were short-handed, and that's part of the story: Zion Williamson sat for rest, Trey Murphy III is out with bilateral patellar tendinopathy, and Yves Missi is out with a knee injury. New Orleans fell to 4-7. But the Warriors' turnaround isn't about one soft opponent — it's an eight-game run that started with a team that looked broken in October and now looks like it never lost the recipe.

The injuries on Golden State's side haven't gone anywhere either. The Warriors have been winning with a thin rotation, leaning on Curry and a supporting cast that keeps filling gaps. Eight straight, a 6-0 homestand, and a piece of history nobody had ever claimed. The 0-3 start is officially ancient history.

Sports · Nov 10, 2026 · 8:36 AM ET

Cooper Flagg drops 43 — the second teenager ever with a 40-10-5 game

By Matt

Cooper Flagg dropped 43 points, 10 rebounds and 6 assists as the Mavericks beat the Pacers 125-122 — becoming just the second teenager in NBA history with a 40-10-5 game, after Kevin Durant.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

Cooper Flagg is 19 years old, and he just had the kind of night that makes the rest of the league check the calendar. Flagg scored a career-high 43 points on 16-of-25 shooting — 3-of-6 from three, 8-of-8 from the line — with 10 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 steals as the Dallas Mavericks beat the Indiana Pacers 125-122 at American Airlines Center on Monday night.

Thirty of the 43 came after halftime. Sixteen came in the fourth quarter, including two 18-foot pull-up jumpers in the final 62 seconds — the second a go-ahead bucket with 26.3 seconds left. Dallas trailed by 13 late in the first half and still found a way, winning its third straight to move to 7-4. It was Flagg's fourth straight double-double.

He didn't do it alone. Kyrie Irving scored 35 points on 7-of-10 from deep, and the two of them combined for 78. Pascal Siakam led Indiana with 29 — 26 of them in the first half, just 3 after the break — and the Pacers still had seven players in double figures and lost. That's the kind of night it was.

The history

The line puts Flagg in company that barely exists. He is the second teenager in NBA history to post 40 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists in a game. The first was Kevin Durant, who went for 42 points, 13 rebounds and 6 assists for Seattle at Golden State on April 16, 2008 — the final game of the 2007-08 season. That was 18 years ago.

It was also Flagg's fifth 40-point game as a teenager, the most in NBA history, and it tied him with LeBron James for the most 35-point games by a teenager, with seven. His 14th 30-point game before turning 20 — LeBron had 20 — and per StatMuse, he's the first teenager ever with 40 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals in a game. He turns 20 on December 21.

The mid-range work is the part that should scare people. Flagg has been doing his damage in tight spaces, off limited dribbles, and Monday night he closed a game from 18 feet — the shot defenses are supposed to be happy to give up. Dallas coach Dusty May called the performance unbelievable for a 19-year-old, and honestly, there isn't a better word for it.

MLB · Nov 9, 2026 · 9:09 PM ET

Red Sox ready to move on from Duran

By Matt

Boston is finally dropping its asking price for Jarren Duran, and USA Today's Bob Nightengale says the outfielder is 'as good as gone' — two years after his All-Star breakout, a .207 season and a projected $11 million arbitration payday have made him the odd man out in a crowded outfield.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Red Sox are finally ready to move on from Jarren Duran — and this time, the price is coming down.

USA Today's Bob Nightengale reported from the General Manager Meetings that Boston will lower its asking price for the outfielder, calling him "as good as gone." The Red Sox have talked about trading Duran for two years, but they have always asked too much. That price figures to drop after a 2026 season in which Duran slashed .207/.266/.361 over 151 games — the second-worst qualifying hitter in baseball.

The math is what changed. MLB Trade Rumors projects Duran to earn roughly $11.1 million in salary arbitration this winter, up from $7.7 million in 2026. Boston does not want to pay that for a player who may be a fourth outfielder, at best.

The outfield that passed him by

This is a roster problem as much as a money problem. Boston views Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu as its preferred long-term starting outfield, leaving Duran on the sideline. There is no starting job for him in Boston anymore, and paying eight figures for a bench bat is not how the Red Sox want to spend.

It is a remarkable fall for a player who was the heart of the team two seasons ago. Duran was a seventh-round pick in the 2018 draft who broke through in 2024 with one of the best seasons in franchise history: a .285/.342/.492 slash line, 21 home runs, 75 RBIs, 191 hits, 34 stolen bases, and a league-leading 48 doubles and 14 triples. He was named an All-Star, won All-Star Game MVP with a go-ahead two-run homer off Hunter Greene — a 413-foot shot that gave the American League the lead for good — and finished eighth in AL MVP voting. He was the first Red Sox player to win All-Star Game MVP since J.D. Drew in 2008, and his 9.0 bWAR was one of the best marks in the game that year.

The slide, in numbers

The decline has been steep and fast. Duran took a step back in 2025, hitting .256 with 16 home runs and 84 RBIs in 157 games — still productive, still leading the AL in triples with 13 — and then fell off a cliff in 2026.

2024: .285; 21; 75; 34; .834

2025: .256; 16; 84; 24; .774

2026: .207; 20; 69; 21; .627

Even the 2026 season had a strange bright spot buried in it: Duran still put together a 20-homer, 20-steal campaign, his second 20-20 season. Only Mookie Betts and Jackie Jensen had ever done that more than once in a Red Sox uniform before him. The power and speed never fully left. The batting average did — and with it, the on-base percentage, the leadoff role, and the everyday job.

What Boston wants — and what happens next

Boston previously sought a frontline starting pitcher in exchange for Duran, and that asking price found no takers. With the price now dropping, the market should open up. The Phillies, Cubs, Mariners, and Rangers have all been linked to Duran in recent months.

The Red Sox have three options: tender him a contract and trade him, tender him and keep him, or non-tender him and get nothing in return. Nightengale's reporting makes the direction clear — the first option, at a price the market will actually pay. Duran is 30 years old and under team control through 2028, so a team acquiring him gets more than a rental. But the team acquiring him is betting that 2024 was the real Duran and 2026 was the outlier, not the other way around.

Two years after he was an All-Star Game MVP, Jarren Duran's time in Boston looks over. The only question left is what the Red Sox get back for him.

Magic's Star Trek Secret Lair superdrop beams in today — five drops, $29.99 each, and a sixth still to come

By Matt

Secret Lair x Star Trek: Set Phasers to Superdrop goes on sale today at noon ET on MagicSecretLair.com — five drops at $29.99 non-foil or $39.99 foil, from full-art lands to a full Klingon-language set, with a sixth drop still unrevealed and the main set landing Friday.

What happened

The transporters are warmed up. Secret Lair x Star Trek: Set Phasers to Superdrop goes on sale today, Monday, November 9, at 9 a.m. PT / noon ET on MagicSecretLair.com, with a pre-queue opening an hour earlier. Wizards of the Coast revealed five of the six drops on October 27. The sixth is still to be revealed.

Each drop costs $29.99 in non-foil or $39.99 in foil, while supplies last. All five revealed drops run $149.95 non-foil or $199.95 foil before tax and shipping, and spending $199.99 earns a foil copy of Return of the Wildspeaker, reskinned as "Transporter Boondoggle." Orders over $99 ship free.

The five drops

New Worlds — full-art basic lands from new worlds, the kind of drop that ends up in decks for years after the set itself is forgotten.

Beam Me Up — the transporter drop, and the cleverest of the five: four reversible cards. Eerie Interlude becomes Beam Us Up, Momentary Blink, Essence Flux becomes Materialize, and Conjurer's Closet becomes The Transporter. Every card in the drop is reversible.

tlhIngan maH — a full Klingon-language set, with Klingon-script cards developed with help from Marc Okrand, the linguist who created the language for the films. This is the one collectors will be talking about longest.

KHAAAAAAAAN — the Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan drop, which Wizards itself notes knows exactly how many A's belong in the title.

Lower Decks — the chaos of Star Trek: Lower Decks, for the people who want their Magic cards to be funny.

Why the timing matters

The superdrop lands four days before the main event: Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek hits tabletop on Friday, November 13, with prereleases running November 6–12 and the MTG Arena release on November 10. All four Commander decks have been revealed, each a ready-to-play 100-card deck with 32 new-to-Magic cards. The set is the next Universes Beyond release, and Wizards is treating it like one — a Secret Lair superdrop, a full Commander lineup, and a set code (TRK) collectors already know by heart.

The business behind it is worth a line, too. Hasbro reported that Magic: The Gathering set a quarterly revenue record of $616.1 million in Q3 2026, up 34 percent year over year, with The Hobbit as the fourth-best-selling set in Magic history and the highest prerelease participation ever for a Universes Beyond set. Star Trek is walking into the biggest moment the game has ever had.

What to watch

Secret Lair sales are queue-based and while-supplies-last, and the pre-queue opens at 8 a.m. PT — an hour before the sale. Adding a drop to your basket does not reserve it, so the drops that sell out will sell out fast, and the Klingon set is the obvious candidate. The unrevealed sixth drop is the other thing to watch: Wizards has not said what it is or when it appears, and a surprise sixth drop in a superdrop like this has a way of becoming the chase card of the whole release.

Set phasers, indeed.

The details

Sale opens: Today, Nov 9 — 9 a.m. PT / noon ET

Pre-queue: 8 a.m. PT / 11 a.m. ET

Where: MagicSecretLair.com

Price: $29.99 non-foil / $39.99 foil per drop

Bonus: Foil "Transporter Boondoggle" per $199.99 spent

Main set: Nov 13 (tabletop), Nov 10 (Arena)

GTA 6 takes over Selfridges in London — 60-plus items, including a £2,500 jacket

By Matt

Selfridges has turned its Bond Street store in London into a Grand Theft Auto 6 takeover, with more than 60 items of merch on sale — including a £2,500 jacket. The game itself lands November 19, and pre-loading opens Tuesday.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

Grand Theft Auto 6 has taken over one of the most famous department stores in the world. Selfridges has opened a GTA 6 activation at its Bond Street store in London, and put the merchandise on sale online on Monday morning, according to VGC. The range runs to more than 60 items — including a £2,500 jacket.

It is the kind of takeover only a game this size gets. GTA 6 is ten days from release, and Rockstar is now putting it in front of people who do not follow gaming news at all: shoppers on Oxford Street, walking past a storefront that has been turned into Leonida.

The countdown is real now

The timing is not an accident. Pre-loading for GTA 6 opens on Tuesday, November 10, and Rockstar has revealed the game's file size ahead of launch. The Selfridges takeover is the physical version of the same rollout. Sixty-plus items is not a capsule — it is a full merch line, with a £2,500 jacket at the top of it. That price tells you who Rockstar thinks is buying: not just players, but collectors who treat GTA merch the way sneakerheads treat a limited drop.

Watch the launch trailer

Austin Reaves drops season-high 43 as Luka-less Lakers hold off Pistons

By Matt

With Luka Doncic sidelined by lower-back tightness, Austin Reaves poured in a season-high 43 points — including a dagger three in the final minute — as the Lakers beat the Pistons 121-116 in Detroit for their fifth straight win. It was his fifth career 40-point game, tying Wilt Chamberlain on the Lakers' all-time list.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Los Angeles Lakers built a 26-point lead, nearly gave it all away, and then watched Austin Reaves take it back. Reaves scored a season-high 43 points as the Lakers beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116 on Sunday night at Little Caesars Arena, improving to 9-2 with their fifth straight win — all of it without Luka Doncic, who sat out with lower-back tightness.

Reaves went 14-of-27 from the field, 4-of-6 from three, and a perfect 11-of-11 at the free-throw line, adding five rebounds and four assists in 37 minutes with just one turnover. The Lakers led 38-14 after one quarter and 61-48 at halftime. Detroit cut the lead to one three times in the fourth quarter. Then Reaves buried an off-balance three-pointer with about 45 seconds left, waved toward the courtside seats, and closed the game out at the line.

The Luka-less pattern

This is becoming a thing with Reaves, and the numbers are almost funny. Sunday was at least the third time he has produced a 40-plus-point game with a Lakers star sidelined — the 51 against Sacramento on October 26, 2025, the 45 against Indiana on February 8, 2025, and now the 43 in Detroit, all with Doncic unavailable. His career high is the 51, set against the Kings — also with Doncic out.

Sunday's game gave him a new line on the franchise's history page, too. The 43 was his fifth career 40-point game, tying Wilt Chamberlain for 12th place on the Lakers' regular-season list. Magic Johnson is next on that list, with six. Reaves is an undrafted guard in his sixth season, and he is now tied with Wilt.

Doncic, the NBA's leading scorer at 40.1 points per game, missed his second game of the season. The Lakers are 2-0 without him. The good news for Los Angeles: Doncic was taken off the injury report and cleared to return for Monday night's game in Atlanta, the second night of the back-to-back. The bad news: Reaves is listed as questionable for that game with an illness, and Quentin Grimes is out with a sprained finger.

The game itself

The Lakers came out like a team that had been waiting to prove a point. They forced eight Detroit turnovers in the first quarter and scored 17 points off them, with Quentin Grimes — starting in Doncic's place — scoring 10 of his 12 points in the opening frame. A Kessler basket at the start of the second quarter made it 40-14, the Lakers' biggest lead of the night.

Detroit did not fold. Daniss Jenkins, a reserve, scored 22 of his career-high 31 points in the first half, including a buzzer-beating three that cut it to 61-48. Kevin Huerter added 24. Cade Cunningham had 14 points but did not make a field goal in the first half, and Duncan Robinson scored 12. The Pistons, the league's top-ranked defense coming in, shot 19-of-48 from three and kept coming — an 11-0 surge in the final 2:04 of the third cut a 13-point deficit to three.

Reaves had words with a courtside fan midway through the game, then spent the rest of the night answering him. He scored 13 in the third quarter to keep the Lakers afloat, then hit the dagger three with 44.5 seconds left and made sure to wave goodbye to the same spectator on his way back down the floor.

The supporting cast held up its end. Ziaire Williams and Collin Sexton each scored 17 off the bench. Walker Kessler had 12 points, 16 rebounds, four assists, and three blocks. The Lakers shot exactly half of their 84 shots. Detroit lost back-to-back games for the first time this season.

What it means

The Lakers are 9-2 and alone in first place in the West, and they just won a road game against the league's best defense without the player averaging 40 a night. That is the whole story. Reaves is not a fill-in anymore — he is a second star who happens to play his best basketball when the first star is in street clothes. The question now is whether the Lakers can keep it rolling with Doncic back in the lineup Monday in Atlanta — and whether Reaves, listed as questionable with an illness, is even available to follow it up.

If Sunday was the answer, Monday is the test.

World of Warcraft: Forever is the biggest launch in WoW history

By Matt

World of Warcraft: Forever launched November 4, and Blizzard says it is the biggest launch in the game's history — by peak concurrent players and returning players — with the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years.

What happened

World of Warcraft: Forever is the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history.

Blizzard announced on Saturday, November 7, that the new version of WoW — which launched globally on Tuesday, November 4 at 3:00 p.m. PST, all regions at once — set records for peak concurrent players and for the highest number of returning players in the game's history. The company did not release exact figures, but the scale of the claim is the point: in a game that has been running for 22 years, this is the biggest launch it has ever had.

Executive producer Holly Longdale added another detail: Forever also drew the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years. And in China, NetEase reported more than one million concurrent players — a record for the game in that region.

What Forever actually is

Forever is the third ongoing version of World of Warcraft, sitting alongside Retail and Classic. It is included in the existing subscription — no separate purchase — and it takes players back to the original 2004 version of Azeroth, with a level cap of 60, plus new zones, quests, dungeons, and raids built on top of that foundation.

The idea is the one Blizzard has been circling for years: the vanilla world, rebuilt with modern systems and new content, for players who want the old map without the old grind. The beta was the largest in franchise history, and the launch itself went smoothly — short queues, no major outages, which for a WoW launch is its own kind of news.

Why the numbers matter

WoW launches are usually measured in two ways: how many people show up, and how many of them stay. Blizzard is only claiming the first one so far — peak concurrents, returning players, new players — and it is not sharing the raw numbers. But the combination is notable: a record for returning players and the most new players in 15 years means Forever is pulling in both directions at once, luring back lapsed players and bringing in people who have never played.

The China number is the most concrete data point. One million concurrent players in a single region, on a single day, is a scale that very few games ever reach. NetEase's record suggests the launch was not just a Western nostalgia event.

What it means

World of Warcraft has been declared dead more times than any game in history, and it keeps answering with launches like this one. Forever is a bet that the original Azeroth — the map, the pace, the world — still has pull, and the first numbers say the bet is paying off. The real test is what happens in a month, when the launch rush fades and the question becomes whether players are still logging in. For now, though, Blizzard can say something it has never said before: this is the biggest launch the game has ever had.

Pokémon printed 10 billion cards a year — and still sold out

By Matt

The Pokémon Company printed roughly 10 billion cards in the fiscal year ending March 2026 — past 85 billion lifetime — and it still wasn't enough. Output has been flat for three years because the printers are already at maximum capacity, and the next big plant doesn't open until 2028.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Pokémon Company printed roughly 10 billion Pokémon TCG cards in the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026. The lifetime total is now past 85 billion cards since the game launched in 1996. The cards are printed in 16 languages and sold in more than 90 countries.

And it still was not enough. Shops are still selling out on day one.

That is the number at the center of the story: 10 billion sounds like a flood, but it is a ceiling. Output has been flat at around 10 billion a year for three years — the high-water mark was about 11.9 billion in fiscal 2023/24 — because the company has been printing at maximum capacity since January 2025. There is no more room on the presses. The only way to make more cards is to build more presses, and that takes years.

The sellout problem

The demand side is not a mystery. A London shop's allocation rose 40% and still sold out on day one, according to a Brit Brief report from a London Comic Con panel on November 6. That is the pattern everywhere: allocations go up, demand goes up faster, and the shelves are empty by the afternoon.

The timing makes it worse. Mega Evolution – Delta Reign and the 30th Celebration set launched on November 6, right into the holiday season, when demand is at its peak. New sets used to be a restock event. Now they are a race, and the race is over before most people get to the store.

The fix is coming — slowly

The Pokémon Company is building a new printing campus: 1.27 million square feet, due for completion in 2027, with full operation expected in late 2028. When it is running, it would roughly double the company's printing capacity.

That is a real fix, and it is also two years away. Between now and then, the math does not change: 10 billion cards a year, flat, against demand that keeps growing. The company is not holding back supply to create hype — it is printing as fast as it physically can, and it is still not enough.

What it means

For collectors, the takeaway is simple: the scarcity is structural, not artificial. The cards are not hard to find because the company is being cute with supply. They are hard to find because the printers are maxed out and the next plant is two years from full operation. That means day-one sellouts are the normal state of things until 2028, and the secondary market is where the action is — for better and for worse.

Ten billion cards a year. Eighty-five billion lifetime. And still sold out. That is the Pokémon economy right now.

NBA · Nov 8, 2026 · 8:01 AM ET

Stephen Curry drops 41 as Warriors win seventh straight in OT over Magic

By Matt

Stephen Curry scored 41 points — including 12 unanswered in the final 2:21 of regulation — as the Warriors beat Orlando 126-119 in overtime for their seventh straight win. At 38, Curry just set the record for most 40-point games by a player 35 or older, and did something no player has done in the tracking era.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Golden State Warriors beat the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night at Chase Center, and Stephen Curry was the whole story — again.

Curry finished with 41 points, six rebounds, and six assists on 13-of-19 shooting, 5-of-10 from three, and a perfect 10-of-10 at the free-throw line. His three-point play with 1:38 left in overtime put the Warriors ahead for good, and his driving hoop 44 seconds later sealed his 41-point night. The Warriors won their seventh straight game. They started the season 0-3. They are now 7-3.

The finish

This game should not have been close. The Warriors led by 16 at halftime, and Orlando — short-handed, 2-7, on a losing streak — had no business being in it. But the Magic exploded for 37 points in the third quarter, and Jamal Cain's putback with two seconds left in regulation sent it to overtime.

Then Curry took over. He scored 12 unanswered points himself in the final 2:21 of regulation, and in the fourth quarter and overtime combined, he went a perfect 4-for-4 on go-ahead shots in the final two minutes. That is the first time in the tracking era — since the start of the 1996-97 season — that a player has made at least four field goals without a miss under those circumstances in a single game. All told, there were six different instances down the stretch when Curry made a shot to either tie the game or take the lead.

Wendell Carter Jr. missed two free throws with 1:15 left in overtime that would have tied it. Curry made sure Orlando never got another chance.

Why this one is historic

The 41 was Curry's second 40-point game this season, and his fourth in his last five games with at least 30 points. It was also his 16th 40-point game since turning 35 years old — breaking a tie with LeBron James for the most in NBA history by a player age 35 or older. Curry is 38.

And there was another milestone buried in the box score: Curry joined Oscar Robertson and Russell Westbrook as only the third point guard in NBA history to record 25,000 points and 5,000 rebounds in his career. He also passed 6,000 career assists, according to Elias.

The streak around him matters too. This is the Warriors' longest winning streak since seven in a row from March 3-15, 2025, and their first seven-game win streak without Jimmy Butler since January and February of their 2022 championship season. The team that started 0-3 and looked finished is now the hottest team in the West.

The help

Curry did not do it alone. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, eight rebounds, and three blocks in his 10th career game — including a key three-pointer in overtime. Brandin Podziemski added 15 points and seven rebounds. Every Warriors player who logged minutes scored, and the bench outscored Orlando's second unit 42-31.

Orlando fought hard — 18 three-pointers, a 24-3 edge on the offensive boards, and Cain's 18 points and 12 rebounds off the bench — but it was the Magic's fourth straight loss, and Curry was the difference between a win and a loss.

What it means

There is a temptation to treat nights like this as routine for Curry. They are not routine. A 38-year-old point guard just went 4-for-4 on go-ahead shots in the final two minutes of regulation and overtime, set the record for 40-point games after 35, and joined two of the greatest point guards ever in a club that only had two members. The Warriors started 0-3. They have won seven straight. And the reason is the same as it has been for a decade: when the game gets tight, Stephen Curry decides it.

Lendeborg: 23 pts, 8 reb, 3 blk

Podziemski: 15 pts, 7 reb

Warriors: 7-3, seven straight wins

Magic: 2-7, four straight losses

Sports · Nov 8, 2026 · 8:00 AM ET

Johnny Walker TKOs Waldo Cortes-Acosta in chaotic UFC Vegas 124 main event

By Matt

Johnny Walker was knocked down in the first round and lost the first two rounds on the scorecards — then landed a question-mark kick, a backfist, and a right hook to become the first man ever to knock out Waldo Cortes-Acosta, stopping him in the third round at UFC Vegas 124.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

Johnny Walker just pulled off the kind of comeback that makes heavyweight MMA the most unpredictable division in the sport.

Walker (24-10 MMA, 10-7 UFC) stopped Waldo Cortes-Acosta (17-5 MMA, 10-5 UFC) by TKO at 2:27 of the third round in the main event of UFC Vegas 124 (UFC Fight Night 293) on Saturday night at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas — becoming the first man ever to knock out Cortes-Acosta.

The finish came out of nowhere, which is exactly how Walker fights. After being knocked down in the first round and losing the first two rounds on MMA Junkie's scorecards (10-9, 10-9 Cortes-Acosta), Walker uncorked a question-mark kick, followed it with a backfist, and then landed the right hook that ended the fight. Cortes-Acosta, who had never been stopped by strikes before, went down and the fight was over.

A short-notice main event that delivered

This fight almost didn't happen — at least not like this. Walker took the main event on nine days' notice after the original headliner, Sean Brady vs. Michael Morales, was canceled when Brady suffered an injury. It was Walker's second heavyweight fight, and his second heavyweight win by knockout: he beat Mick Parkin by first-round KO in October.

That is the Johnny Walker experience in a nutshell. He is chaos in human form — a light heavyweight who moved up to heavyweight and has now finished both of his fights there by knockout, in a division where one clean shot ends everything. He was losing this fight. Clearly losing it. And then he wasn't.

Cortes-Acosta's loss is his third straight, after defeats to Alexander Volkov and Curtis Blaydes. The man who had never been knocked out now has that on his record, and the man who did it was supposed to be the short-notice replacement.

The co-main

In the co-main event, Tatiana Suarez beat Virna Jandiroba by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28), a strong performance in a strawweight fight with title implications. Suarez controlled the fight on the scorecards, and the win keeps her firmly in the mix at 115 pounds.

What it means

Walker is now 2-0 at heavyweight with two knockouts, and he did it the hard way — taking a fight on nine days' notice, getting dropped early, and finishing a man who had never been finished by strikes. Heavyweight is a division where momentum is everything, and Walker just grabbed a fistful of it. The question now is who the UFC matches him with next, because a heavyweight who can end a fight from anywhere, at any moment, is appointment viewing — even when he's losing.

The result

Winner: Johnny Walker (24-10 MMA, 10-7 UFC)

Loser: Waldo Cortes-Acosta (17-5 MMA, 10-5 UFC)

Method: TKO (punches), Round 3, 2:27

Event: UFC Vegas 124 (UFC Fight Night 293), Meta APEX, Las Vegas

Co-main: Tatiana Suarez def. Virna Jandiroba by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

NBA · Nov 7, 2026 · 5:08 PM ET

Celtics set NBA Cup record with 24 threes

By Matt

Jayson Tatum dropped 34 points in 29 minutes and Boston buried an NBA Cup-record 24 threes in a 119-80 rout of the Hornets — a wire-to-wire blowout that pushed the Celtics to 7-2 and 2-0 in Cup play.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Boston Celtics routed the Charlotte Hornets 119-80 on Friday night at Spectrum Center, and the score barely tells the story. Boston led 40-20 after the first quarter, by 31 at halftime, and by as many as 46 points on the way to its second NBA Cup group-play win.

Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 34 points in just 29 minutes — he did not play a minute in the fourth quarter — and the Celtics made 24 three-pointers on 54.5% shooting from deep. That is a new NBA Cup record.

The win moved Boston to 7-2 on the season and 2-0 in East Group C, where the Celtics now lead the group by record and own a +53 scoring differential — 44 points clear of the next team.

The three-point blitz

The record was not a late-game accident. Boston hit 17 threes in the first half alone, tying a franchise record, and kept firing until the 24th fell. The Celtics finished 24-of-44 from deep (54.5%) with 33 assists as a team.

They were even flirting with bigger history. The NBA record for most threes in a game is 29 — a mark the Celtics themselves tied on Opening Night in 2024 against the Knicks. They settled for the Cup record instead, and with the game long decided, there was no reason to chase it.

The contrast on the other end was stark. Charlotte shot 11-of-50 from three (22%) and 27-of-92 from the field overall (29.3%) in its second-lowest scoring performance of the season. The loss was the Hornets' sixth straight, dropping them to 3-7.

Tatum's night

Tatum did most of his damage before halftime: 24 of his 34 points came in the first two quarters, including 18 in the first. He finished 9-of-16 from the field, 5-of-8 from three, and a perfect 11-of-11 from the free-throw line, with 8 rebounds, 9 assists, a steal, and a team-best plus-36.

The road crowd in Charlotte even gave him MVP chants — fitting for a player who averages nearly 30 points per game against the Hornets, the most he averages against any of the 29 other teams.

It is also worth remembering how recently this version of Tatum was in doubt. He returned from a torn Achilles tendon on March 6 of last season, and nights like this one — efficient, unhurried, done by the fourth quarter — are the clearest sign yet that the explosion and the shot-making are fully back.

He had help. Derrick White added 18 points, including 10 in the first quarter, with 4 threes, 5 assists, and 4 rebounds. Payton Pritchard came off the bench for 12 points and 4 more threes. Tatum was the only player on either side to reach 20 points.

The box score

Final score: Celtics 119, Hornets 80

Celtics threes: 24-44 (54.5%) — NBA Cup record

Hornets threes: 11-50 (22.0%)

Tatum: 34 PTS, 8 REB, 9 AST, 9-16 FG, 5-8 3PT, 11-11 FT, +36

White: 18 PTS, 4 REB, 5 AST, 4-6 3PT

Pritchard: 12 PTS, 4-7 3PT

Team assists: 33

Celtics record: 7-2 (2-0 in NBA Cup group play)

Hornets record: 3-7 (sixth straight loss)

Around the game

• Brandon Miller: Charlotte's night got worse when Miller left the game with a groin injury.

• First stop on the road: the game opened a four-game road trip for Boston.

• Cup math: point differential matters in NBA Cup group play, and Boston's +53 through two games is the best in East Group C by 44 points.

• Next Cup game: Boston's next group-play game is not until Tuesday, Nov. 24, against the Wizards.

What it means

This was a statement in the exact form the NBA Cup rewards: win big, and the tiebreaker takes care of itself. The Celtics did not just beat an injury-riddled, struggling Hornets team — they buried them from three, sat their star for the fourth quarter, and still walked out with the best point differential in their group.

The bigger signal is Tatum. A 34-point night in 29 minutes, with the efficiency and the bounce, against a team he has always torched, says the Celtics' best player is rounding into form at the same time the team is stacking wins. Boston's next test is a real one: at Milwaukee on Sunday night.

What's next

Boston visits the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8 p.m. at Fiserv Forum.

Red Sox predicted to sign Freddy Peralta for $92M

By Matt

Sports Illustrated's Nicholas Selbe predicts Boston lands Freddy Peralta on a four-year, $92 million deal — a bet on the ace's Tampa turnaround after Sonny Gray elected free agency.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The prediction

The Red Sox need a starter, and one of the offseason's biggest names is being linked to Boston. Sports Illustrated's Nicholas Selbe predicted the Red Sox will sign Freddy Peralta to a four-year, $92 million contract this offseason.

The fit is obvious. Sonny Gray has elected free agency, leaving a hole at the top of Boston's rotation. Peralta is a two-time All-Star and one of the top arms on the open market — and after a wild 2026, his value is trending back up at exactly the right time.

The Jekyll-and-Hyde season

Peralta's 2026 was a tale of two teams. He opened the year with the New York Mets, where it went sideways: a 5-9 record and a 4.99 ERA in 22 appearances. A deadline trade to Tampa Bay changed everything.

With the Rays, Peralta went 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 appearances, allowing just three earned runs over his final six regular-season starts — a 0.79 ERA down the stretch. Overall for the season, he finished 10-11 with a 4.42 ERA and 156 strikeouts in 32 games.

Then came October. Peralta was named ALCS MVP after posting a 0.75 ERA over three appearances (12 innings) against Cleveland, helping the Rays reach the World Series against his old club, Milwaukee.

New York Mets: 5-9; 4.99; —

Tampa Bay Rays: 5-2; 3.25; —

Full season: 10-11; 4.42; 156

Why Boston believes in the Tampa version

The Rays version of Peralta is the one Boston would be paying for — and it's not hard to see why. A year earlier, in his final season with the Brewers, Peralta went 17-6 with a 2.70 ERA and 204 strikeouts, finishing fifth in NL Cy Young voting. That is the track record underneath the messy Mets half-season: a durable, strikeout-heavy starter with 30 starts in four consecutive years.

The question for Boston is which version shows up in 2027. The case for the Red Sox: the Tampa turnaround wasn't a small sample blip. It was a full second-half reset — a 3.25 ERA, a dominant closing stretch, and an ALCS MVP — from a 30-year-old entering his age-31 season who has done this before.

The competition

Boston won't be alone in the bidding. MLB Trade Rumors' Steve Adams predicted Peralta lands with the Chicago Cubs on a five-year, $110 million deal, and the Blue Jays, Giants, Padres, White Sox, and Orioles have all been named as fits. Spotrac has floated a seven-year, $201 million projection, while The Athletic's Jim Bowden predicted five years and $140 million.

Selbe's $92 million over four years would be the shorter, cheaper end of that range — a bet that Boston can land the ace without going to the nine-figure lengths other suitors might. Whether Peralta takes a shorter deal or chases the longer one is the open question of his winter.

What it would mean for Boston

If the prediction holds, the Red Sox would be buying a proven top-of-the-rotation arm to replace Gray — and keeping him away from the rest of the AL East in the process. The Rays aren't expected to re-sign him at this price, and every team in the division knows what the Tampa version of Peralta looks like. Boston landing him would be a statement that the rotation hole gets filled with a real ace, not a stopgap.

Ocarina of Time remake is 2026's highest-rated game — a 96 on Metacritic

By Matt

Nintendo's ground-up Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched November 5 to a 96 Metascore — the highest-rated game of 2026, and one of the 30 highest-rated games in Metacritic history.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is back, and the critics have spoken about as loudly as critics can speak. Nintendo's ground-up remake for Switch 2 launched Thursday, November 5, 2026, carrying a 96 on Metacritic — the highest-rated game of 2026, built from 87 critic reviews with zero mixed or negative notices among them. Players agree so far: the user score sits at 9.6.

The remake is a Switch 2 exclusive, $59.99 digital and $69.99 physical. It is, by the numbers, one of the best-reviewed games ever made — sitting inside Metacritic's all-time top 30, one rung below the original it remakes.

The original is still the one to beat

Here is the beautiful problem with remaking Ocarina of Time: the 1998 Nintendo 64 original holds a 99 on Metacritic, still the highest aggregate score the site has ever recorded for any game. The remake's 96 doesn't topple its own legend. It does, however, clear Nintendo's last attempt by a comfortable margin — Ocarina of Time 3D on the 3DS sits at 94 — and it puts the remake ahead of every other 2026 release, including Resident Evil Requiem, Phantom Blade Zero, Forza Horizon 6, and The Witcher 3 Remastered.

The review spread tells the story. The Guardian, Eurogamer, GamesRadar, and Destructoid all handed out perfect scores. IGN, GameSpot, and Forbes each gave it 9 out of 10. One outlet's verdict, quoted widely this week, called it "the gold standard for any remake of any franchise going forward."

What Nintendo actually built

This is not a remaster. Nintendo rebuilt the game from the ground up for Switch 2, with overhauled visuals across every dungeon and landmark, reworked camera and movement controls, new character dialogue, and a symphonic orchestral soundtrack. It targets and holds 60 frames per second in both docked and handheld modes, and it integrates with the Nintendo Switch App's Zelda Notes service for interactive maps and progress tracking.

There are new additions for returning players, too. A new Hall of Fallen Foes lets players view statues of the enemies they have defeated — a small touch, but the kind that tells you the developers were thinking about people who have already beaten this game three times and want a reason to do it a fourth. Nintendo's own Ask the Developer interview, published around launch, goes deep on just how much work the rebuild took.

Not everything made the cut. The lack of Master Quest — the harder alternative dungeon mode included in previous releases — is the most common complaint in otherwise glowing reviews.

Launch week had its wrinkles

No launch this big goes perfectly. Within hours of release, the remake had been dumped and run on a PC emulator, continuing a pattern that has shadowed Nintendo's biggest Switch 2 launches. And some Amazon physical pre-orders were delayed by up to a week after launch day, leaving buyers waiting while the digital version went live on schedule.

Neither wrinkle has dented the reception. At 96, the remake is also the most critically acclaimed game on Switch 2 to date — a remarkable achievement for a game that first came out before a lot of today's Switch 2 owners were even born.

Steam Drops Four Free Games to Keep

By Matt

Four very different indie games — led by the 99%-rated Heartfall — are free to download and keep on Steam starting today.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Steam's newest round of free games is live starting today, November 6, 2026 — four games, free to download and keep forever. No catch, no subscription, no time limit on claiming them. Just add them to your library and they're yours.

This is part of a steady stream of free games Steam has delivered throughout 2026, and this week's set is a strong one: a story-driven visual novel RPG, a cosmic-horror cooking game, a found-footage horror short, and a post-apocalyptic tactical RPG. Four very different experiences, and every one of them carries an overwhelmingly positive rating from Steam users.

The four free games

Heartfall: A Tale in Three Lives: 99% positive; Story-driven visual novel RPG

Cucina Stellata: 97% positive; Psychological horror cooking game

Playable Archive: 97% positive; First-person found-footage horror

Outcast Tales: 95% positive; Post-apocalyptic tactical RPG

Heartfall: A Tale in Three Lives — 99% positive

The headliner of the set, and the highest-rated game of the four. Heartfall is a story-driven visual novel RPG from developer Kazehita that follows a character named Grian after he wakes up on a mysterious island. Players explore different storylines, form alliances, uncover secrets, and make decisions that change how the adventure unfolds.

The scale is what stands out: it's a fan project inspired by the YouTube series 3rd Life, featuring over 400,000 words of dialogue, 450 illustrations, and more than 50 original music tracks. A 99% positive rating puts it among the highest-rated free games on Steam — the kind of number usually reserved for established classics, not a free fan project.

Cucina Stellata — 97% positive

The weirdest game in the set, and maybe the most interesting. Developed by Filthy Eden and published by CRITICAL REFLEX, Cucina Stellata is a psychological horror experience that combines traditional Italian cooking with cosmic horror. Players prepare authentic 19th-century Italian recipes in what the game describes as "a kitchen haunted by hunger."

It starts out looking like a straightforward cooking game, then descends into disturbing imagery and strange supernatural elements. It's currently sitting at 97% positive across more than 1,100 Steam reviews, and it's short — about an hour — which makes it an easy weekend pickup.

Playable Archive — 97% positive

For horror fans looking for something different, Playable Archive is a first-person adventure from DarkStone Digital built around mysterious footage of a New England couple who discover a strange object while renovating their home. Players investigate disturbing events — demonic rituals, communicating with the dead — across multiple timelines.

The whole game runs 30–60 minutes and has to be completed in a single sitting, which fits the found-footage format perfectly. It also holds a 97% positive rating on Steam.

Outcast Tales — 95% positive

The final game in the set is something completely different: a post-apocalyptic tactical RPG with turn-based combat and roguelite mechanics. Developed by Hardlane Studio, it has players leading a dysfunctional crew of survivors through a dangerous wasteland filled with mutants, robots, and hostile raiders.

The hook is a personality system that lets characters develop friendships, rivalries, and even romantic relationships based on player decisions. Add in customizable character classes, strategic combat, and Twitch integration, and there's plenty here to keep you busy. It carries a 95% positive rating on Steam.

Why this batch is worth grabbing

Free-game drops on Steam are nothing new, but a set where the lowest-rated game still sits at 95% positive is rare. These aren't throwaway titles — they're four polished indie games across four genres, and the price of admission is zero. Whether you're hunting for something to play this weekend or just adding to the ever-growing backlog, all four are worth claiming while they're free.

MLB · Nov 6, 2026 · 2:08 PM ET

Red Sox open to trading Duran and Yoshida

By Matt

With Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu, and Ceddanne Rafaela locked in as the starting outfield, the Red Sox are open to moving Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida this offseason.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The Boston Red Sox are open to trading Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida this offseason. That's the word from Alex Speier of The Boston Globe, reported by Bleacher Report, as Boston looks to improve a roster that struggled down the stretch and was swept in the AL Wild Card round.

The reason is simple: the outfield is crowded, and the future is already set. Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu, and Ceddanne Rafaela are the starting outfield, all under team control through at least 2029. That leaves Duran and Yoshida, as Speier put it, in "a familiar state of limbo."

"With that trio in place for years, Duran and Yoshida reside in a familiar state of limbo," Speier wrote. "Either can contribute but the Sox are open to moving one or both."

The logjam

Boston has five outfielders for three spots, and the three who are staying are the three youngest and cheapest. Anthony, Abreu, and Rafaela are locked in for years. Duran and Yoshida are the odd men out — both useful, neither with a clear everyday role anymore.

Duran played 151 games in 2026 in large part because Anthony was unavailable for so much of the season. If Anthony had been healthy, Duran's role would have been a talking point for months. Yoshida, meanwhile, has been squeezed into a left field / designated hitter platoon that doesn't really have room for him either.

Duran: the fascinating, frustrating trade chip

Duran is the harder call. His ceiling is high and his floor is what makes teams hesitate.

He was an All-Star in 2024 and won the All-Star Game MVP award, hitting .285/.342/.492 with 21 home runs and 34 steals that season. Then came the slide. He hit just .207/.266/.361 in 151 games in 2026 — but still went 20/20, with 20 home runs and 21 steals.

That's the paradox of Duran's trade value right now: the power-speed combination is still there, but his chase and whiff rates soared in 2026 and his batting average cratered. His value is at an all-time low even after a 20/20 campaign, and the Sox have flirted with dealing him for two years now.

The money complicates it further. Duran turned 30 on September 5 and has two years of arbitration remaining before free agency. He's projected to earn about $11 million in 2027 through arbitration — an eight-figure salary for a player without an everyday role. The Sox may decide they'd rather sell low than carry that number.

Still, teams looking for outfield help would almost certainly have interest. A 30-year-old with 20/20 ability, two years of control, and a track record of an All-Star season is a real trade chip, even coming off a down year. Back in 2025, the San Diego Padres reportedly offered a package including ace Dylan Cease and elite catching prospect Ethan Salas for Duran, per Sean McAdam of MassLive — a reminder of what his value looked like before the slide.

Yoshida: the contract is the problem

Yoshida's situation is more straightforward, and harder to solve. He's entering the final season of the five-year, $90 million contract he signed to come over from Japan after seven seasons with the Orix Buffaloes. He has $18.6 million remaining on the deal.

He hit .274/.347/.399 in 87 games in 2026 — respectable numbers, but he's played just 142 games over the last two seasons, and at $18.6 million for a part-time DH, the contract is the obstacle. As MassLive's Chris Cotillo put it, Yoshida "looks like a goner" — Boston could try to trade him again, something it hasn't had luck with before, or simply cut bait and eat the money.

The Sox need to add a power bat this winter, and they'll need somewhere to play him. Moving Yoshida — or Duran — is how that spot opens up.

What it means for the offseason

This isn't a fire sale. It's a roster squeeze with a clear logic: three young outfielders are set, two veterans are in the way, and Boston needs to upgrade elsewhere — power, pitching, or both.

The open question is what the return looks like. Duran's value is depressed after 2026, and Yoshida's contract limits his market. The Sox will explore both markets, and how aggressive they get may depend on how much they need the money and the roster spot for the bigger moves they want to make.

One thing is clear: it would be a surprise if Boston entered the 2027 season with the same outfield it had in 2026.

Collectibles · Nov 6, 2026 · 7:54 AM ET

Pokémon TCG enters the National Toy Hall of Fame

By Matt

Thirty years after it debuted in Japan, the Pokémon Trading Card Game is a Hall of Famer — inducted Thursday alongside bingo, Care Bears, and the playground slide.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

The Pokémon Trading Card Game is officially a member of the National Toy Hall of Fame. The Strong National Museum of Play in Rochester, New York, announced the 2026 class on Thursday, November 5, on the Today show — and Pokémon TCG made the cut in its first year as a finalist.

It joins three other inductees: bingo, Care Bears, and the playground slide. The four winners came out of a field of 12 finalists that also included Bop It!, Mahjong, Monster High dolls, Mouse Trap, Polly Pocket, Sorry!, Tickle Me Elmo, and Yahtzee. All four are now enshrined and on display at The Strong.

Thirty years, 85 billion cards

The timing is the story. The Pokémon TCG debuted in Japan in 1996 — thirty years ago this year — after the Game Boy games turned monster-collecting into a phenomenon. The Hall of Fame, established in 1998, recognizes toys that "have inspired creative play and enjoyed popularity over a sustained period." Few inductees can match this one on the sustained part: the game has never really left the cultural conversation since.

The numbers back it up. As of March 2026, more than 85 billion Pokémon cards have been printed and distributed worldwide. The Strong's own write-up calls the game "renowned for its relative accessibility compared to other collectible card games" — a big reason it spread from schoolyards to a global hobby that now supports grading companies, billion-dollar resale markets, and release-day lines at every major retailer.

"Pokémon TCG's widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," curator Mirek Stolee said in the announcement.

A very good week to be a Pokémon collector

The induction lands on the same week as the biggest release day of the anniversary year. Mega Evolution—Delta Reign hits shelves today, November 6, alongside the final wave of 30th Celebration collections. It is the kind of week that shows exactly why the Hall of Fame came calling: thirty years in, the game is still setting release-day records instead of coasting on nostalgia.

The other inductees tell their own version of the same story. Bingo descends from an Italian lottery played around 1530 and is now played virtually worldwide. Care Bears, like Pokémon, got a boost from an active fan community that mobilized around the nomination. And the slide — the simplest toy on the list — was honored for its role in child development and a century of playground use.

What to watch

The Strong says the induction will likely lead to new exhibits and events around the Pokémon TCG in the new year. For collectors, the near-term watch is simpler: this is the third piece of institutional recognition the hobby has picked up in a year when the cards themselves keep breaking records. The game is not just popular. It is, officially, historic.

God of War Laufey delayed to May 20, 2027

By Matt

Santa Monica Studio pushed God of War Laufey from February 16 to May 20, 2027 — three more months of polish for Faye's first outing as the series lead, still a PS5 exclusive.

What happened

Santa Monica Studio is delaying God of War Laufey by three months. The game was set to launch February 16, 2027. It will now arrive May 20, 2027, still as a PlayStation 5 exclusive.

The studio announced the move Wednesday, November 4, in a short statement on X. No specific problem was named — the extra time, the studio said, goes to "putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential." More updates are promised soon, with no date attached to them.

The timeline

This one moved fast from reveal to release date, which makes the delay sting a little less — and a little more.

• June 2026: Revealed at PlayStation's State of Play, closing the show. Faye — Laufey, Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother — wakes after her own funeral in the Everywhen, an afterlife where gods from different mythologies cross paths. Deborah Ann Woll plays Faye; Jack Quaid voices Phranque, a gelatinous cube traveling with her.

• July 2026: The February 16, 2027 date is confirmed at San Diego Comic-Con.

• September 29, 2026: Pre-orders open, with a Standard Edition and a Digital Deluxe Edition.

• November 4, 2026: The delay to May 20, 2027 — 93 days later.

That is a quick turnaround from announcement to launch by modern standards, and the February date lasted barely four months. If you pre-ordered, the studio's statement says nothing about pre-order terms, bonuses, or editions changing — treat those as unchanged until Sony says otherwise.

Why it matters

Laufey is the first God of War where you do not play Kratos. Faye leads, with a legendary sword, a Serpent's Bow, and combat built around speed and vertical movement — a deliberate break from the weightier Norse games. The reveal trailer ran more than 20 minutes of uncut gameplay, and it introduced two gods standing in Faye's way: Sekhmet and Begtse.

Santa Monica has done this before. God of War Ragnarök slipped from 2021 to November 2022 under similar "polish" framing, and it went on to be one of the best-reviewed games of its year. A 93-day delay this late in the cycle reads like a game that is content-complete and needs optimization and bug fixes — not a rescue job.

The new date also buys breathing room. February 2027 is crowded — Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis lands February 12, Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold on February 23 — and Sony's own Until Dawn 2 arrives January 28. May is, for now, a much quieter month.

Godzilla stomps into Apex Legends on November 10 — a Storm Point Wildcard takeover, a heat-ray Devotion, ten kaiju Legend skins, and a mythic Dorsal Dagger, running through December 1.

Godzilla is coming

Godzilla is stomping into Apex Legends. Respawn announced the Apex Legends | Godzilla Event today, November 5, and it runs November 10 through December 1 — three weeks of the King of the Monsters tearing up Storm Point. The tagline says it all: survive the monster, become a monster.

This is not a skins-only crossover. Godzilla is on the map, and you cannot kill it. You can only survive it.

Storm Point becomes Godzilla's stomping ground

The centerpiece is a Wildcard takeover of Storm Point. The map is mid-attack: damaged buildings, burnt trees, fallen signs, and destruction scattered across the island, with Godzilla looming above it all.

When Godzilla marks an area for destruction, a countdown starts before its Heat Ray strikes. Players brave enough to run into the blast zone before the beam hits can grab a Care Package holding a custom Devotion — a heat-ray weapon that tracks enemies on hit. It is the one piece of Godzilla's power you can actually take for yourself.

There is also a new Kaiju Zone on Storm Point to explore for Kaiju Energy, Kaiju Crates, and kaiju-themed finishers.

Ten Legends are getting Godzilla-themed skins drawn from across the franchise, including some deep cuts: Octane, Fuse, Ash, Horizon, Wattson, Ballistic, Valkyrie, Wraith, Loba, and Sparrow. The monsters represented include Godzilla, Mechagodzilla, Mothra, and Destoroyah.

The headline prize is the Dorsal Dagger, a new Universal Mythic Melee inspired by one of Godzilla's dorsal fins, with a matching Deathbox. It is Wraith's first mythic melee and the game's second universal mythic melee. Nine Legendary weapon skins are in the mix too, for the Devotion, Hemlok, Rampage, CAR, Havoc, Longbow, Wingman, Prowler, and Sentinel.

The Godzilla Event Pass runs on challenges: the free track earns rewards like the Jet Jaguar Octane skin and Godzilla Event Packs, while the Premium Track (950 Apex Coins) unlocks the Iconic Ghidorah 1991 Catalyst skin, the Legendary Gravity Beam Prowler skin, Epic Apex Packs, and more. Twitch Drops run November 10–17 with select creators.

The event is tied to Godzilla's return to theaters — Godzilla Minus Zero hits theaters this week, with a 3D re-release in IMAX and large format on November 6. The timing is no accident: the movie brings the monster back to the big screen, and Apex brings it to the Outlands the same week.

Respawn teased this one first. On November 2, the official Apex account posted a 17-second clip captioned "Something big is coming…" — a glowing Apex logo splitting into a row of shapes that turned out to be Godzilla's dorsal plates, with a roar at the end. Three days later, the full reveal landed.

• Dates: November 10 – December 1, 2026

• Mode: Wildcard takeover on Storm Point

• Headline weapon: custom Heat Ray Devotion from blast-zone Care Packages

• Skins: 10 kaiju Legend skins, 9 Legendary weapon skins

• Mythic: Dorsal Dagger universal melee + matching Deathbox

• Platforms: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, PC (Steam, EA App, Epic Games Store)

GameStop's $10,000 Pokémon pack gives you a 44.8% chance of pulling a card worth $6,000–$8,000

By Matt

GameStop's new Riptonium Power Pack costs $10,000 for one PSA-graded Pokémon card — and GameStop's own odds say nearly 75% of pulls come back worth less than the pack. The top chase is a $156,000 Lugia.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

GameStop has gone all in on the digital pack. The retailer announced Riptonium on October 10 — its biggest Power Pack tier yet — and the price is exactly what it sounds like: $10,000 for a single digital pack that reveals one PSA-graded Pokémon card.

The catch is right there on GameStop's own listing. According to the odds GameStop publishes for the pack, 44.8% of pulls land in the $6,000–$8,000 estimated value band. That is at least $2,000 less than the pack costs, before resale fees or the gap between an estimate and what a buyer can actually get for the card.

The odds, straight from GameStop

Here is the full value chart for Riptonium, as reported from GameStop's listing:

$6,000–$8,000: 44.8%

$8,000–$10,000: 29.9%

$10,000–$20,000: 22.9%

$20,000–$40,000: 1.5%

$40,000–$80,000: 0.5%

Above $80,000: 0.4%

Add it up and 74.7% of pulls come back worth less than the $10,000 pack price. Only 2.4% of pulls land above $20,000. The top pull currently listed is valued at $156,000 — a PSA 10 2005 #105 Lugia ex-Holo, per Resell Calendar's report on the pool.

GameStop warns on the listing that values can fluctuate and that the probabilities update every five minutes. The estimates are calculated from market data and feed GameStop's instant buyback offers, which pay 90% of the estimated value. So even a "break-even" pull at $10,000 is worth $9,000 the moment you take the buyback.

How Power Packs work

Riptonium is the top rung of a ladder GameStop has been building all year. Power Packs are digital mystery packs made in partnership with PSA: you buy a pack online, it opens digitally to reveal a real, physical, PSA-graded card, and that card goes into your PSA Vault — a secure, insured storage facility in Delaware — until you decide to ship it, sell it, or keep it stored. Every card was already graded and slabbed before you spent a dollar.

The platform launched to the public on April 15, 2026 with four categories — Pokémon, football, basketball, and baseball — and nine price tiers: Starter ($25), Silver ($50), Gold ($100), Sapphire ($250), Platinum ($500), Diamond ($1,000), Lunar ($2,500), Neutronium ($5,000), and Riptonium ($10,000). Higher tiers buy a deeper card pool and a higher ceiling. The category list has since grown to include One Piece and themed Pokémon packs like Rewind and On Fire.

GameStop added the $5,000 Neutronium tier after announcing its bid for eBay, and Riptonium now pushes the ceiling to $10,000. It is, by a wide margin, the most expensive single digital pack in the hobby.

Why people are buying it anyway

The math says most buyers lose money. The hobby says that was never the point.

Power Packs sell the rip — the moment of the reveal, live on a creator's stream, with a real slab on the line. GameStop publishes live pull data, so collectors can watch in real time what other people are hitting. And for the 0.4%, there is a $156,000 Lugia sitting at the top of the pool.

That is the same logic that has powered the hobby's biggest nights all year, from Logan Paul's $1.2 million vintage rip to the record $16.49 million Pikachu Illustrator sale. The difference is that GameStop has industrialized it: nine tiers, published odds, a vault, and a buyback button. The casino is open, the odds are printed on the door, and the line is still forming.

VeeFriends goes luxury: the Treasure Chest packs gemstone pins and graded coins into 5,555 boxes for Black Friday

By Matt

Gary Vaynerchuk's VeeFriends is going physical in the biggest way yet — a premium Treasure Chest with sapphire gemstone pins, NGC graded coins, and Super Stickers, limited to 5,555 boxes and launching Black Friday.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

VeeFriends is ushering in a new era of premium collecting. The Gary Vaynerchuk-founded brand has unveiled the all-new physical Treasure Chest, a luxury collectible box that launches on Black Friday — and with only 5,555 chests in existence, it is the most exclusive VeeFriends Super Stickers and pin release yet.

Each Treasure Chest holds a randomized assortment of four premium collectibles, built around 21 VeeFriends characters. This is not another sticker drop. This is VeeFriends dressing up for the high-end shelf.

What's inside

Every chest contains four treasures, each featuring one of 21 possible VeeFriends characters:

• Sapphire gemstone pins framed in 18K gold plating

• NGC graded coins crafted in various metals, including pure silver and gold

• Debut Super Stickers in new sapphire colorways

• Classic pins

The scarcity is the point. Every collectible inside the chest — except the coins — is limited to 99 or fewer. The 5,555 chests break down into 555 sealed cases of 10 boxes each, and the sealed-case sale is the only chance to buy a case as a case.

How the sale works

The release rolls out in five waves, and the order matters — holders get first crack, the public gets last:

• Wave 1 — Sealed case sale: Monday, November 24 at 12 p.m. ET through Tuesday, November 25. Exclusive to select Series 1 holders, based on an account snapshot taken Monday, November 24 at 9 a.m. ET. One case per account. Price: $1,999.99 (43% off). Cases ship starting Friday, November 28.

• Wave 2 — Series 1 holder sale: Tuesday, November 25 at 12 p.m. ET through Wednesday, November 26, if inventory remains.

• Wave 3 — Series 2 and Iconics holder sale: Wednesday, November 26 through Friday, November 28 at 12 p.m. ET, if inventory remains. Price: $249.99 (29% off). Boxes ship the week of December 3.

• Wave 4 — Black Friday weekend live breaks: Friday, November 28 through Monday, December 1. VeeFriends goes live to break 55 reserved cases on Whatnot.

• Wave 5 — Public sale via EQL: Week of December 3, if inventory remains.

Series 1 Spectacular holders of the 21 featured characters also get a two-week window to claim one Treasure Chest. Hobby retailers have the box listed for preorder at $399.95, with a 10-box case at $3,989.95.

Why this one matters

VeeFriends started as an NFT project, but its physical collecting arm has been building for years. The Super Stickers line debuted at The National Sports Collectors Convention in July 2023, and the brand has been steadily turning its characters into real, hold-in-your-hand collectibles ever since — including a Spectacular Series boxed sticker set whose public pre-order draw ran November 4–5 at $99 a box, and a Monster Squad collaboration with Crocs for Halloween.

The Treasure Chest is the loudest statement of that direction yet: gemstones, gold plating, graded coins, and a print run smaller than most card-shop allocations. It lands as VeeFriends approaches its five-year anniversary in 2026, and as the brand takes a bigger live role in the hobby — VeeFriends joins Goldin, TikTok, and AFA at the Coins, Cards & CHAOS live shopping event at Valley Forge Casino Resort in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, on November 14–15.

For collectors, the math is simple. There are 5,555 boxes, a holder-first sale ladder, and a public window that only opens if anything survives. If the Treasure Chest sells the way VeeFriends' last few drops have, the week of December 3 may not come at all.

Call of Duty: Warzone ends on PS4 and Xbox One on November 6

By Matt

When Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 starts on Friday, Warzone stops working on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One — ending the battle royale's run on the consoles it launched on.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

What happened

Call of Duty: Warzone is ending support on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on Friday, November 6, when Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 begins. From that point on, the battle royale will no longer be playable on either last-gen console.

It is the end of an era in the most literal sense. Warzone launched on PS4 and Xbox One in March 2020, and for more than six years those consoles have been its home base. Season 1 moves the game exclusively to current-generation hardware — PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC — and November 6 also marks the first time Warzone is available on a Nintendo console.

What Season 1 brings

The new season is not just a platform cull. It adds 33 new weapons from Modern Warfare 4 and introduces a new battle royale map, Hajin, as the game enters its next chapter.

For players still on last-gen hardware, though, the headline is simple: one more day. Warzone remains playable on PS4 and Xbox One through Thursday, November 5. After the Season 1 update lands, that is it.

The last-gen farewell tour

Sony gave the PlayStation 4 one last nod this week, releasing system firmware 14.02 on November 4 — a security-only patch, with no new features. It is the kind of quiet maintenance update a console gets when the industry has already moved on.

The timing is hard to ignore. GTA VI arrives on PS5 on November 19, and PlayStation has already pushed the PS5 firmware update required to play it. The last generation is not being switched off overnight, but the biggest games are done building for it.

Warzone's departure is the clearest marker yet. When the most-played free-to-play shooter on the planet stops supporting your console, the generation is over in every way that matters.

What to do if you still play on PS4 or Xbox One

If Warzone is your game and you are still on last-gen, Friday is the deadline to make a plan — upgrade to a current-gen console or PC, or find your next game. Your account, progress, and unlocks carry over to current-gen platforms, so nothing you have earned is lost. Only the old hardware is being left behind.

Dead by Daylight Removes TheBurntPeanut's Free Content in a Second, Longer Statement

By Matt

Behaviour Interactive has removed the Dead by Daylight content gifted to streamer TheBurntPeanut, saying it moved too fast and broke trust — and its second statement, posted November 3, lays out exactly what it says went wrong and what changes now.

Dead by Daylight's Halloween-weekend controversy has a second chapter. Behaviour Interactive has now removed the in-game content it gifted to Twitch streamer TheBurntPeanut, and its longer follow-up statement — posted November 3 on the main Dead by Daylight account — admits the studio moved too fast, skipped its own checks, and broke trust with its community.

This is a follow-up to our November 2 post on the first apology. That first statement, posted November 1 on the smaller DbD Pulse account, said the gift was made without appropriate approvals. The new statement, a four-page post, is Behaviour's attempt to answer the questions players were actually asking.

What happened

On October 30, during a Halloween stream, TheBurntPeanut played Dead by Daylight for the first time. Members of Behaviour's team noticed a very large audience in the game's Twitch directory watching a streamer who had not played it before, and saw a chance to welcome new players.

A staff member then gifted TheBurntPeanut access to the game's DLC characters, perks, and in-game currency during the livestream. When TheBurntPeanut offered to give the content back, concerned about the backlash to come, the official account replied in stream chat: "WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT! THEY ARE YOURS TO KEEP!"

The backlash that followed had two layers. Critics raised concerns about Behaviour partnering with TheBurntPeanut, pointing to clips from his past streams, and many players objected to the dismissive tone of the official account's reply. Some players said they uninstalled the game as the dispute escalated.

What Behaviour says it got wrong

The November 3 statement breaks the failure into three parts, in the studio's own framing:

Due diligence. The decision to give the creator in-game content and join his chat was made before taking the necessary time to look at whether it was a good idea. It happened quickly and outside the team's usual discussions. Behaviour says it normally looks thoroughly at a new creator's past content to judge whether they represent the values of inclusion its community expects. In this case, it says, that was not taken into proper consideration or discussed as a group.

Internal process. The studio says it did not have stringent enough processes and guardrails to prevent in-game items from being granted directly to players without larger consensus and approval. A team member acted without a supporting system behind them to guide them to another outcome.

Communication standards. The "WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT!" reply, along with some other messages in that session, showed a disregard for the context the team was suddenly in and crossed the line of appropriate responses from the brand, Behaviour says. That reply escalated the situation for the studio and for the community, especially for content creators on the frontlines of those conversations, and that was unacceptable.

Behaviour also states its values in the post: respect, transparency, diversity, and creating a space where people from different backgrounds and experiences feel welcome. Diversity is one of Dead by Daylight's core principles, it says, and when it chooses to work with a creator, it is putting its name next to theirs.

What is changing now

• The content is gone. Behaviour says it has already removed the content that was granted to the creator.

• Creator guidelines are being rewritten. That includes how the team interacts with creators playing Dead by Daylight, who on the team can make those calls, and how to identify creators whose past conduct is in direct opposition to the inclusive community Behaviour says it is trying to build.

• Approval methods are being updated. Request and approval methods for granting content and currency to players are being reworked, with checks and balances at the right time, and the team will be trained on the new processes.

• Creator Program rules are being enforced directly. Creators found to have violated Creator Program policy will result in removal. Any hold or removal will be communicated directly to the creator involved, with no additional communications on social channels or in program Discords. All removals are at the team's discretion.

• Internal action is confidential. Behaviour says it takes the situation very seriously and is taking appropriate action internally, but as a confidential matter it will not share further details.

The statement closes with a direct admission: "This incident has broken trust with our community who hold expectations and regards for the types of people we partner with, but more importantly expectations of the conduct and actions taken by our team in our daily work within this community. We understand it will be a slow road to regain that trust but we are committed to doing the work necessary to get there."

The response, by the numbers

The November 3 statement post itself drew a large reaction on X, with 11K comments, 4.4K reposts, and 28K likes at the time of the screenshots shared for this story — a measure of how widely this one is still being watched, not a verdict in itself.

TheBurntPeanut has also responded on stream, saying he saw the reaction online and noting a refund request that cited the collaboration and the communication team's response. He said he did not think he had said anything about transgender people in the last two to two-and-a-half years of streaming, and asked whether he ever had. That response is his, not Behaviour's, and the underlying allegations from critics remain allegations about past clips, not findings in Behaviour's statement — which focuses on its own process, not on adjudicating the streamer's history.

Why this one matters professionally

Strip away the noise and this is a process story, which is exactly why it is worth covering straight. Giving a creator a sneak peek at content is not unusual in itself — Behaviour's own first statement notes that. What made this one different, by Behaviour's own account, was speed without approval, a check that never happened, and a public reply that poured fuel on it instead of slowing it down.

The test now is not the statement. It is the next time a big streamer drops into the Fog: who approves the gift, what check happens first, and whether the public response matches the values the studio just restated.
